inputs.name: class
inputs.description: Extra classes merged onto the accordion wrapper, after the base `w-full`. Item borders come from `<ui-accordion-item>`, not here.

inputs.name: collapsible
inputs.description: Whether clicking the open item in `'single'` mode closes it, leaving nothing open. Defaults to `true`; set `false` to force one item to always stay open. Ignored when {@link type} is `'multiple'`, where items always toggle closed.

inputs.name: openValues
inputs.description: Values of the items to open. Applied whenever the array *reference* changes, overwriting whatever the user had open — pass a new array to drive the accordion, and leave it `null` (the default) for uncontrolled use. It is not two-way: user toggles via {@link toggle} are not written back here.

inputs.name: type
inputs.description: `'single'` (default) keeps at most one item open — opening one closes the rest; `'multiple'` lets any number stay open and makes {@link collapsible} irrelevant. Also reinterprets {@link openValues}: in `'single'` only its first entry is honoured.

inputs.name: class
inputs.description: Extra classes merged onto the panel, after the base `overflow-hidden text-sm`. The inner `pb-4 pt-0` padding wrapper is not affected — override spacing on the projected content itself.

inputs.name: class
inputs.description: Extra classes merged onto the item wrapper, after the base `border-b` — set e.g. `border-none` on the last item.

inputs.name: content
inputs.description: Body text for simple mode, rendered as plain text inside the built-in panel. Only read when {@link title} is set; for markup or components, project a `<ui-accordion-content>` instead.

inputs.name: skeleton
inputs.description: Renders a placeholder header bar instead of the item, for loading states. Takes precedence over both modes: neither {@link title} nor any projected trigger/content is rendered, and the item cannot be opened.

inputs.name: title
inputs.description: Simple mode — supplying a title makes the item render its own trigger button and panel, and any projected `<ui-accordion-trigger>` / `<ui-accordion-content>` is ignored. Leave it undefined to compose those sub-components yourself.

inputs.name: value
inputs.description: Key identifying this item in the parent accordion's open set and in `[openValues]`. Required, and must be unique within the accordion — duplicates open and close together.

inputs.name: class
inputs.description: Extra classes merged onto the trigger button. The base classes include the `[&[data-state=open]>svg]:rotate-180` rule that flips the chevron, so keep any override additive rather than replacing the selector-based styling. Vertical padding is not in the base set — add your own (e.g. `py-4`) to match simple-mode items.

inputs.name: open
inputs.description: Two-way bound visibility. Nothing inside `ui-alert-dialog-content` exists in the DOM while this is `false`. Unlike `ui-dialog`, clicking the backdrop does not clear it — only Escape, the action/cancel buttons or your own code can.

outputs.name: open
outputs.description: Two-way bound visibility. Nothing inside `ui-alert-dialog-content` exists in the DOM while this is `false`. Unlike `ui-dialog`, clicking the backdrop does not clear it — only Escape, the action/cancel buttons or your own code can.

inputs.name: class
inputs.description: Extra classes merged onto the inner `<button>`, after the primary-button defaults — pass e.g. `bg-destructive hover:bg-destructive/90` to style a destructive confirmation.

inputs.name: class
inputs.description: Extra classes merged onto the inner `<button>`, after the outline-button defaults (which include the `mt-2 sm:mt-0` offset for the footer's stacked-on-mobile layout).

inputs.name: actionText
inputs.description: Override for the action button text. When unset, falls back to the locale's `continue` string.

inputs.name: cancelText
inputs.description: Override for the cancel button text. When unset, falls back to the locale's `cancel` string.

inputs.name: class
inputs.description: Extra classes merged onto the centred panel (not the backdrop). Overrides the default `max-w-[calc(100vw-2rem)] sm:max-w-lg` sizing when you pass a width utility.

inputs.name: description
inputs.description: Simple-mode sub-heading. Only rendered when {@link title} is also set.

inputs.name: locale
inputs.description: Locale dictionary or registry key. Falls back to `UI_LOCALE_ID` when not set.

inputs.name: title
inputs.description: Simple mode: renders the header **and** a footer with ready-made cancel / action buttons wired to {@link cancelClick} and {@link actionClick}. Leave it unset to project your own header and footer — with no title neither the header nor the default buttons are rendered, and {@link description}, {@link actionText} and {@link cancelText} have no effect.

outputs.name: actionClick
outputs.description: The confirm button was pressed. Only emitted by the simple-mode footer (i.e. when {@link title} is set) — project your own `ui-alert-dialog-action` and you handle its click yourself. The dialog closes itself either way, so do not also call `hide()`.

outputs.name: cancelClick
outputs.description: The cancel button was pressed. Same simple-mode-only rules as {@link actionClick}.

inputs.name: class
inputs.description: Extra classes merged onto the host. The variants set colour and layout only; note the built-in `[&>svg]` rules already absolutely position a leading icon and indent the text past it.

inputs.name: description
inputs.description: Simple-mode body text under the title. Only rendered when {@link title} is also set; on its own it is ignored.

inputs.name: title
inputs.description: Simple-mode heading. Supplying it switches the alert to the generated layout — title, optional {@link description}, then any projected content — instead of pure projection. Leave it empty to compose `ui-alert-title` / `ui-alert-description` yourself.

inputs.name: variant
inputs.description: Severity treatment. Also drives the announcement semantics: `'default'` renders as `role="status"` / `aria-live="polite"`, `'destructive'` as `role="alert"` / `aria-live="assertive"`, which interrupts a screen reader — so reserve it for genuine errors.

inputs.name: class
inputs.description:
Extra classes merged onto the description host. Any nested `

` already gets relaxed leading, so multi-paragraph bodies need no extra styling.

inputs.name: class
inputs.description: Extra classes merged onto the title host. Renders as a plain styled `<div>`, not a heading element — add your own `<h2>`/`<h3>` inside if the alert needs to appear in the document outline.

inputs.name: class
inputs.description: Extra classes merged onto the chart container, which already carries `relative w-full`.

inputs.name: curve
inputs.description: Interpolation along the top edge of each area (and its outline stroke). `'linear'` (default) uses straight segments, `'monotone'` an overshoot-free cubic spline (degrading to linear for a two-point series), `'step'` holds each value until the next x. When {@link stacked} is on, only the upper edge is curved — the lower edge is retraced with straight segments to close the band, so tall curves can leave a visible seam.

inputs.name: dir
inputs.description: Layout direction. `'auto'` (default) resolves from the host element's inherited DOM direction after view init; `'ltr'`/`'rtl'` force it. RTL reverses the x range (first category on the right) and moves the y tick labels to the opposite edge. See {@link isRtl}.

inputs.name: fillOpacity
inputs.description: Alpha of each area's fill, 0–1. The default 0.25 keeps overlapping unstacked series legible; raise it towards 1 for stacked charts, where bands don't overlap. The outline stroke is always drawn fully opaque, so `0` yields a line chart with the areas' colours.

inputs.name: height
inputs.description: Height of the SVG in px, applied literally (not scaled). It is also the y-axis extent: values are mapped between `height - 28` and `12` in user space, leaving the bottom band for the category labels.

inputs.name: series
inputs.description: One filled area per series. Points are matched across series **by position**, not by name: the x axis categories are taken from the *first* series' `data[].name`, so every series should carry the same number of points in the same order. Each entry's `color` overrides the palette colour picked from the series index; `id` (falling back to `name`) is the key used by the legend and {@link toggleSeries}, so give series unique names when they have no `id`. Array order is paint order — and when {@link stacked} is on, stack order: the first series sits at the bottom. The y domain always starts at 0 and is nice-rounded over the *visible* series, so negative values fall outside the plot.

inputs.name: showCrosshair
inputs.description: Draw the vertical line marking the hovered category, spanning the plot area.

inputs.name: showGrid
inputs.description: Draw the dashed horizontal gridline behind each y tick. The tick *labels* are drawn either way.

inputs.name: showLegend
inputs.description: Render the legend below the chart. It is interactive: clicking an entry calls {@link toggleSeries}, so hiding it also removes the only built-in way to unhide a series.

inputs.name: showTooltip
inputs.description: Show the shared tooltip listing every visible series at the hovered category. Values are the series' raw numbers, never the stacked or percent-normalized ones. Hover still emits {@link pointHover} when disabled.

inputs.name: stacked
inputs.description: Stack the areas cumulatively instead of overlaying them on a shared zero baseline. Overlaid areas (default) let {@link fillOpacity} show the series behind; stacked areas read as parts of a whole and make the y domain the per-category *total*. See {@link stackingMode}.

inputs.name: stackingMode
inputs.description: How {@link stacked} areas are normalized. `'absolute'` (default) stacks raw values; `'percent'` rescales each category to sum to 100, pinning the y domain to 0–100 so the chart fills the plot regardless of totals. Ignored when {@link stacked} is false.

inputs.name: title
inputs.description: Human-readable chart name, used only to prefix the container's accessible summary ("<title>. Area chart with N data points.").

inputs.name: width
inputs.description: Fallback width of the SVG user-space coordinate system, in px, used until the host has been measured — from then on the `viewBox` tracks the host's real width, so user space maps 1:1 to CSS px and the areas never stretch. The measurement needs a block-level box: an inline-block container collapses the `width:100%` SVG, which is why the host is `class: 'block'` and the container `w-full`.

outputs.name: pointHover
outputs.description: Emitted with the nearest category's point from the first *visible* series on pointer move, and with `null` on pointer-leave. `index` is the category index, so consumers can mirror the highlight across their own series. There is no click output — the areas are not interactive targets.

inputs.name: ratio
inputs.description: Width-to-height ratio of the reserved box, expressed as `width / height` (e.g. `16 / 9` for widescreen, `1` — the default — for a square). The box always fills the available width and derives its height from this value via a percentage `padding-bottom`, so the space is reserved before the projected content loads and no layout shift occurs.

inputs.name: class
inputs.description: Extra classes merged onto the bordered trigger container (not the popover).

inputs.name: debounceTime
inputs.description: Milliseconds to delay {@link searchChange} by, so a request per keystroke is avoided. Defaults to `0` (emit synchronously from {@link onInput}). Only the outgoing event is delayed — {@link searchTerm} and therefore the highlight and the client-side {@link filter} update immediately. NOTE: the debounce window is captured once in the constructor, before inputs are set, so any value passed in behaves as `0` (asynchronous but not actually delayed).

inputs.name: disabled
inputs.description: Disables the text box and swallows container clicks, focus-opening and every {@link onKeydown} branch. OR-ed with the reactive-forms disabled state (see {@link setDisabledState}) by {@link isDisabled}, so a template `disabled="true"` cannot be re-enabled by `FormControl.enable()`.

inputs.name: displayWith
inputs.description: Maps an option to the text shown in the chip / closed input and to the string {@link filter} matches against. Defaults to `String`, which is only useful for primitive options — pass e.g. `o => o.name` for objects, otherwise every row renders as `[object Object]`.

inputs.name: filter
inputs.description: Whether the built-in client-side filter hides options that do not contain {@link searchTerm} (case-insensitive substring on {@link getSearchValue}). Set to `false` for server-driven search, where {@link options} is already the result set and hiding it again would double-filter.

inputs.name: locale
inputs.description: Locale dictionary or registry key. Falls back to `UI_LOCALE_ID` when not set.

inputs.name: multiple
inputs.description: Switches to chip/tag selection: picking an option toggles it in the value array instead of replacing it, the popover stays open, the search box is cleared and refocused, each selection renders as a removable `ui-badge` (see {@link removeItem}), and Backspace on an empty search box pops the last chip. Also changes what {@link valueChange} emits — an array rather than a single option or `null`.

inputs.name: options
inputs.description: The full candidate list. Every option is rendered as a `ui-command-item` up front and hidden client-side by the `ui-command` substring filter — the list is not virtualised, so keep it to a few hundred entries or drive it server-side by narrowing `options` in response to {@link searchChange} and setting {@link filter} to `false`. Options are tracked by {@link getTrackBy}, so two options with the same {@link getValue} collapse into one tracked row.

inputs.name: placeholder
inputs.description: Override for the placeholder. Falls back to the locale's `selectPlaceholder`.

inputs.name: searchTerm
inputs.description: Two-way bindable query text. Drives the highlight (`highlight` pipe) and, when {@link filter} is on, which options stay visible. Reset to `''` after any selection and whenever the popover closes ({@link onOpenChange}), so a value written into it does not survive a dismiss. Writing to it does not emit {@link searchChange}.

inputs.name: value
inputs.description: Uncontrolled-style seed for the selection, applied by an `effect` whenever it changes: an array replaces the whole selection, a non-array becomes a single-item selection, `undefined` leaves the current selection alone. Setting it from outside does *not* emit `valueChange`. Prefer `ngModel` / `formControl` ({@link writeValue}) — mixing both means the last writer wins. Being a `ModelSignal` is what makes this component a valid Signal Forms `FormValueControl`, and it doubles as the `valueChange` output: Angular derives the output from the model, so there is no separate declaration. Note that after a `writeValue` from a reactive form this still reads the pre-write value — {@link internalValue} is the rendered selection.

inputs.name: valueAttribute
inputs.description: Name of the property that identifies an option, e.g. `'id'`. When set, selection, de-duplication and {@link writeValue} compare `option[valueAttribute]` and the control emits… still the whole option object (see {@link updateValue}) — this input only changes *comparison*, not the emitted shape. When omitted, options are compared by reference, so a form value that is a structurally-equal-but-distinct object will not match any option and renders via `String(value)`.

outputs.name: searchChange
outputs.description: The raw text typed by the user, for server-side search. Fires only from {@link onInput} — never when a selection clears the box, when the popover closes, or when {@link searchTerm} is set programmatically. Delayed by {@link debounceTime}.

outputs.name: searchTerm
outputs.description: Two-way bindable query text. Drives the highlight (`highlight` pipe) and, when {@link filter} is on, which options stay visible. Reset to `''` after any selection and whenever the popover closes ({@link onOpenChange}), so a value written into it does not survive a dismiss. Writing to it does not emit {@link searchChange}.

outputs.name: value
outputs.description: Uncontrolled-style seed for the selection, applied by an `effect` whenever it changes: an array replaces the whole selection, a non-array becomes a single-item selection, `undefined` leaves the current selection alone. Setting it from outside does *not* emit `valueChange`. Prefer `ngModel` / `formControl` ({@link writeValue}) — mixing both means the last writer wins. Being a `ModelSignal` is what makes this component a valid Signal Forms `FormValueControl`, and it doubles as the `valueChange` output: Angular derives the output from the model, so there is no separate declaration. Note that after a `writeValue` from a reactive form this still reads the pre-write value — {@link internalValue} is the rendered selection.

inputs.name: alt
inputs.description: `alt` text for the simple-mode image. Leave empty for purely decorative avatars.

inputs.name: class
inputs.description: Extra classes merged onto the host. The default size (2.5rem, density-scaled) comes from the component's own CSS, so a `size-`/`h-`/`w-` utility here overrides it; the roundness and `overflow-hidden` are also merged from here.

inputs.name: fallback
inputs.description: Text shown while the image loads and, permanently, if it fails — typically initials. Rendered on its own when there is no {@link src}; without either, the component falls back to projected content.

inputs.name: loading
inputs.description: Overlays a translucent scrim and spinner on top of the avatar. Independent of image load state.

inputs.name: skeleton
inputs.description: Placeholder mode: renders a pulsing round skeleton *instead of* the avatar, ignoring {@link src}, {@link fallback} and projected content. Note the skeleton is a fixed 2.5rem, so it does not follow a size override on {@link class}.

inputs.name: src
inputs.description: Image URL for simple mode. When set, the projected `<ng-content>` is ignored entirely — use either `src`/{@link fallback} or `ui-avatar-image` / `ui-avatar-fallback` children, not both.

inputs.name: class
inputs.description: Extra classes merged onto the fallback disc (`bg-muted`, centred, full-size) — where you set the initials' text size or a custom background. The element renders only while the parent avatar's image has not loaded, and always when there is no `ui-avatar-image` at all.

inputs.name: alt
inputs.description: `alt` text; leave empty when the avatar is decorative and the name is already in the DOM.

inputs.name: class
inputs.description: Extra classes merged onto the `` (default `aspect-square h-full w-full`) — e.g. `object-top` to change the crop anchor.

inputs.name: src
inputs.description: Image URL. Required — for the input-driven form use `ui-avatar`'s own `src` instead.

inputs.name: class
inputs.description: Extra classes merged onto the host; padding/size utilities go here since the variants set colour only.

inputs.name: label
inputs.description: Convenience text content. When non-empty it is rendered *instead of* any projected content, so use one or the other — projection is the escape hatch for icons or markup inside the badge.

inputs.name: skeleton
inputs.description: Renders a fixed-size {@link SkeletonComponent} placeholder in place of the badge and drops all variant styling, for loading states that must not shift layout.

inputs.name: variant
inputs.description: Colour treatment from {@link badgeVariants}. `'outline'` is the only one without a filled background — it keeps the inherited surface and just draws the border and `text-foreground`. Ignored while {@link skeleton} is true.

classes.name: BannerComponent
classes.description: Persistent, page-level announcement bar — the slot `alert` (inline, within content) and `toast` (transient) do not fill. Two modes, per the library's projection contract: pass {@link message} for the plain-text case, or project your own content (a link, a button) and it replaces the message entirely.

inputs.name: class
inputs.description: Extra classes merged onto the host.

inputs.name: dismissible
inputs.description: Render a close control that hides the banner and emits {@link dismissed}. Accepts the bare-attribute form (`<ui-banner dismissible />`).

inputs.name: locale
inputs.description: Locale dictionary or registry key, used for the dismiss button's label.

inputs.name: message
inputs.description: Plain-text announcement. Ignored when content is projected into the banner — the projection wins so you can mix text with a link or button.

inputs.name: variant
inputs.description: Severity treatment. Also drives the announcement semantics: everything except `'destructive'` announces politely via `role="status"`; `'destructive'` uses `role="alert"` / `aria-live="assertive"`, which interrupts a screen reader — reserve it for genuine failures.

outputs.name: dismissed
outputs.description: Emits once when the user closes a {@link dismissible} banner.

inputs.name: backButtonText
inputs.description: Label of the breadcrumb's back button, for localisation. Only visible while drilled down.

inputs.name: barGap
inputs.description: Gap between adjacent columns, in px of user space. Column width is whatever is left of the plot area after the gaps, so raising this on a dense series narrows the columns rather than widening the chart.

inputs.name: barRadius
inputs.description: Corner rounding of each column rect, in px (SVG `rx`). Use `0` for square corners.

inputs.name: class
inputs.description: Extra classes merged onto the chart container, which already carries `relative block w-full`.

inputs.name: data
inputs.description: The top-level series: one column per entry, drawn in array order (mirrored in RTL). `name` labels the category axis, `value` is the column height, and the optional `color` overrides the palette colour picked from the index. An entry whose `drilldown` holds the `id` of an entry in {@link drilldownSeries} becomes clickable and navigates into that series — a `drilldown` id with no matching series is inert (see {@link hasDrilldown}). Values are assumed non-negative: the scale is anchored at 0.

inputs.name: dir
inputs.description: Layout direction. `'auto'` (default) resolves from the host element's inherited DOM direction after view init; `'ltr'`/`'rtl'` force it. RTL mirrors the column order, swaps the axis gutter to the right-hand edge and flips the breadcrumb's back chevron. See {@link isRtl}.

inputs.name: drilldownSeries
inputs.description: The child series reachable from {@link data}, keyed by `id`. The list is flat and navigation is exactly one level deep — a click inside a child series never drills further, so child points need no `drilldown` id. Each series' `name` becomes the breadcrumb caption while it is open ({@link currentSeriesName}).

inputs.name: height
inputs.description: Design height of the SVG coordinate system, in px. Combined with the measured width it fixes the `aspect-ratio`, so the chart keeps its proportions while scaling — height is never measured from the DOM. It covers the SVG only; the breadcrumb row adds its own height above it.

inputs.name: showBreadcrumb
inputs.description: Render the breadcrumb row — the {@link backButtonText} button plus the current series name. It only appears while drilled down; hiding it leaves {@link onDrillUp} as the only way back, so wire your own control if you turn it off.

inputs.name: showGrid
inputs.description: Draw the dashed value-axis gridlines behind the columns, one per {@link axisTicks} entry.

inputs.name: showTooltip
inputs.description: Show the floating tooltip for the hovered/focused column, which also carries the "Click to drill down" hint on drillable columns. Hover still emits {@link barHover} when disabled.

inputs.name: showValues
inputs.description: Print each column's formatted value (see {@link formatValue}) above the column.

inputs.name: title
inputs.description: Human-readable chart name. Used to prefix the SVG's accessible summary and, at the top level, as the breadcrumb caption — it falls back to `'Overview'` when unset. See {@link currentSeriesName}.

inputs.name: width
inputs.description: Design width of the SVG user-space coordinate system, in px, and the fallback until the host element has been measured. The rendered SVG is `width="100%"` with this as its `max-width`, so the chart scales down inside narrow containers but never past this width. The host must be a block-level box — an inline-block parent collapses a `width:100%` SVG, which is why the container carries `w-full` and the host `class: 'block'`.

outputs.name: barClick
outputs.description: Emitted for every column click or Enter/Space activation, at either level — including columns that also trigger {@link drilldown}. `index` is the position within the currently displayed series.

outputs.name: barHover
outputs.description: Emitted with the column on hover/focus and with `null` on mouse-leave/blur, so consumers can mirror the highlight.

outputs.name: drilldown
outputs.description: Emitted after the chart has navigated into a child series, carrying the target `seriesId` and the clicked parent point. {@link barClick} fires first for the same click.

outputs.name: drillup
outputs.description: Emitted after {@link onDrillUp} returns the chart to the top-level {@link data}.

inputs.name: barGap
inputs.description: Gap between adjacent bars, in px of user space. Bar thickness is whatever is left of the plot area after the gaps, so raising this on a dense series shrinks the bars rather than widening the chart.

inputs.name: barRadius
inputs.description: Corner rounding of each bar rect, in px (SVG `rx`). Use `0` for square corners.

inputs.name: class
inputs.description: Extra classes merged onto the chart container, which already carries `relative block w-full`.

inputs.name: data
inputs.description: One bar per entry, drawn in array order (left-to-right, or right-to-left when {@link isRtl} resolves true). `name` is the category label under the axis, `value` the bar length, and the optional `color` overrides the palette colour that would otherwise be picked from the entry's index. Values are assumed non-negative: the scale is anchored at 0 and only the maximum is derived from the data, so negative values fall outside the plot.

inputs.name: dir
inputs.description: Layout direction. `'auto'` (default) resolves from the host element's inherited DOM direction after view init; `'ltr'`/`'rtl'` force it. RTL mirrors the bar order, swaps the axis padding, and moves the tick labels to the opposite edge. See {@link isRtl}.

inputs.name: height
inputs.description: Design height of the SVG coordinate system, in px. Combined with the measured width it fixes the `aspect-ratio`, so the chart keeps its proportions while scaling — height is never measured from the DOM.

inputs.name: orientation
inputs.description: `'vertical'` (default) grows bars upward from the category axis; `'horizontal'` grows them sideways with categories stacked down the side. Also switches the aria description between "Column chart" and "Bar chart".

inputs.name: showGrid
inputs.description: Draw the dashed value-axis gridlines behind the bars, one per {@link axisTicks} entry.

inputs.name: showTooltip
inputs.description: Show the floating tooltip for the hovered/focused bar. Hover still emits {@link barHover} when disabled.

inputs.name: showValues
inputs.description: Print each bar's formatted value (see {@link formatValue}) at the end of the bar.

inputs.name: title
inputs.description: Human-readable chart name, used only to prefix the SVG's accessible summary.

inputs.name: width
inputs.description: Design width of the SVG user-space coordinate system, in px, and the fallback until the host element has been measured. The rendered SVG is `width="100%"` with this as its `max-width`, so the chart scales down inside narrow containers but never past this width. Note the host must be a block-level box — an inline-block parent collapses a `width:100%` SVG, which is why the container carries `w-full` and the host `class: 'block'`.

inputs.name: xAxisLabel
inputs.description: Caption centred under the chart. Setting it also reserves extra bottom padding for the text.

inputs.name: yAxisLabel
inputs.description: Caption rotated along the value axis; flips to the right-hand edge in RTL.

outputs.name: barClick
outputs.description: Emitted when a bar is clicked, or activated with Enter/Space while focused.

outputs.name: barHover
outputs.description: Emitted with the bar on hover/focus and with `null` on mouse-leave/blur, so consumers can mirror the highlight.

inputs.name: animationDuration
inputs.description: Milliseconds each frame is held during playback, and also the CSS transition duration applied to the bars and labels — so it doubles as the tween length: the movement finishes exactly as the next frame arrives. Changing it mid-playback takes effect on the next scheduled step.

inputs.name: autoPlay
inputs.description: Start playing on init, without waiting for a {@link play} call or a click on the toolbar button. Read once, shortly after construction.

inputs.name: barGap
inputs.description: Vertical gap between bars, in px of user space. The gaps are taken out of the plot height before it is divided by {@link maxBars}, so raising this shrinks the bars rather than growing the chart.

inputs.name: barRadius
inputs.description: Corner rounding of each bar rect, in px (SVG `rx`). Use `0` for square corners.

inputs.name: class
inputs.description: Extra classes merged onto the chart container, which already carries `relative block w-full`.

inputs.name: dir
inputs.description: Layout direction of the plot. `'auto'` (default) resolves from the host element's inherited DOM direction after view init; `'ltr'`/`'rtl'` force it. RTL grows the bars from the right edge and moves the name/value labels to the opposite sides. Independent of the container's `dir` attribute, which follows the {@link locale} dictionary. See {@link isRtl}.

inputs.name: frameLabels
inputs.description: Caption shown above the chart for each frame, matched to {@link frames} by index; a missing entry falls back to `Frame N`. The first and last entries are also printed as the end captions of the timeline slider, so leave this empty to hide those.

inputs.name: frames
inputs.description: The whole race: one entry per time step, each holding that step's `{ name, value, color? }` points. Only the frame at {@link currentFrameIndex} is drawn — it is sorted by `value` descending and cut to {@link maxBars}, so array order within a frame is irrelevant and bars re-order as values change. Names are the identity across frames: a point keeps its palette colour (assigned on first sight, or from its own `color`) and its `track` identity for the CSS transition, so reusing the same names between frames is what makes bars slide instead of pop. The value axis is rescaled per frame to 110% of that frame's largest value, so lengths are relative within a frame, not across the race.

inputs.name: height
inputs.description: Design height of the SVG coordinate system, in px. Combined with the measured width it fixes the `aspect-ratio`, so the chart keeps its proportions while scaling — height is never measured from the DOM. It is also the budget split between {@link maxBars} bars and {@link barGap} gaps.

inputs.name: locale
inputs.description: Locale dictionary or registry key. Falls back to `UI_LOCALE_ID` when not set.

inputs.name: loop
inputs.description: On reaching the last frame, jump back to the first and keep playing instead of stopping. With `false` (default) playback halts there and {@link animationComplete} fires; when looping that event never fires.

inputs.name: maxBars
inputs.description: How many bars to show — the top N of each frame by value; the rest are dropped. Also the divisor for bar thickness: the plot height is split into exactly this many slots whether or not the frame has that many points, so raising it thins every bar.

inputs.name: title
inputs.description: Human-readable chart name, used only to prefix the SVG's accessible summary.

inputs.name: width
inputs.description: Design width of the SVG user-space coordinate system, in px, and the fallback until the host element has been measured. The rendered SVG is `width="100%"` with this as its `max-width`, so the chart scales down in narrow containers but never past this width. The host must be a block-level box — an inline-block parent collapses a `width:100%` SVG, which is why the container carries `w-full` and the host `class: 'block'`.

outputs.name: animationComplete
outputs.description: Emits once when playback runs off the last frame and stops. Never emitted while {@link loop} is `true`, and not emitted by {@link pause}.

outputs.name: frameChange
outputs.description: Emits the new {@link frames} index whenever the displayed frame changes — from playback, {@link reset}, {@link goToFrame} or the timeline slider — so external captions can stay in step. {@link goToFrame} emits even when the requested index resolves to the frame already shown, so the stream can repeat a value.

inputs.name: borderRadius
inputs.description: Corner radius applied to every widget. Bare numbers are taken as px.

inputs.name: class
inputs.description: Extra classes merged onto the grid container, after the built-in `grid w-full relative` utilities.

inputs.name: cols
inputs.description: Number of columns in the track. Also the divisor used to convert pointer coordinates into grid cells, so changing it re-interprets existing {@link DashboardItem.x} values rather than rescaling them. Fixed at all viewport widths — the grid does not collapse to fewer columns on mobile.

inputs.name: columnWidth
inputs.description: Width of one column. Keep the default `'1fr'` for a fluid grid, which renders as `minmax(0, 1fr)` tracks; any other value (px/rem/%) is used verbatim as the track size. The same value drives the pointer-to-cell maths, so the rendered grid and drop targeting always agree.

inputs.name: editable
inputs.description: Master switch for every edit affordance: drag, resize handles, selection, context menus and drops. Turning it off also clears the current selection (and emits an empty {@link selectionChange}) and hides the cell grid overlay.

inputs.name: gap
inputs.description: Gutter between cells. Counted into the drag/resize snap step, so a wrong value here makes items land one cell off. Bare numbers are taken as px.

inputs.name: itemPadding
inputs.description: Inner padding of each widget. It eats into the cell, it does not grow it — set `0` when a projected component paints edge to edge.

inputs.name: items
inputs.description: The widgets to lay out. **The grid never mutates this array** — every drag, resize, merge, split, add and delete emits the next array through {@link itemsChange} and the consumer must store it and feed it back here. Coordinates are 1-based CSS-grid line numbers, not zero-based indices.

inputs.name: resizeHandleType
inputs.description: Which resize grips a selected widget shows: the four corners, the four edges, or (default) both. Only affects the handles rendered — {@link onResizeStart} still supports all eight directions.

inputs.name: rowHeight
inputs.description: Height of one row, as `grid-auto-rows`. A bare number or numeric string is taken as px. Feeds the drag/resize snap step together with {@link gap}.

inputs.name: showBorders
inputs.description: Draws the outline around each widget. Purely cosmetic — hit-testing and the drop preview are unaffected.

outputs.name: componentInit
outputs.description: Fires once per dynamically rendered widget whose `content` is a component type, handing over its `ComponentRef` for imperative wiring the `inputs`/`outputs` maps cannot express.

outputs.name: externalDrop
outputs.type: { widgetId: string, targetId: string | null, x?: number, y?: number }
outputs.description: A widget dragged in from outside was dropped. `x`/`y` carry the target cell only when the drop landed on empty canvas; when it landed on an existing widget you get `targetId` and no coordinates. The payload comes from the drag source's `application/json` data (`{ type: 'widget', id }`) — the grid adds nothing to {@link items} itself, the consumer must.

outputs.name: itemsChange
outputs.description: The complete next layout after a drag, resize, merge, split, delete or add. The grid does **not** persist it — store it and feed it back through {@link items}, or the widget snaps back on the next change detection. Neighbours overlapped by the moved item are shrunk (or dropped entirely when they cannot shrink), so the array may be shorter than the one you passed in.

outputs.name: selectionChange
outputs.description: The ids currently selected, after every {@link toggleSelection} / {@link clearSelection} and whenever {@link editable} goes false.

classes.name: BentoGridStatWidgetDemoComponent
classes.description: A dynamically-projected demo widget used to show `DashboardItem.content` accepting an arbitrary `Type<unknown>` (not just plain text).

inputs.name: class
inputs.description: Extra classes merged onto the card, after the built-in border/padding/hover utilities.

inputs.name: rowSpan
inputs.description: How many grid rows the card spans (`grid-row: span N`).

inputs.name: span
inputs.description: How many grid columns the card spans (`grid-column: span N`). Static markup only — this item is not the one `ui-bento-grid` drags and resizes; that one is driven by {@link BentoGridComponent.items}.

inputs.name: class
inputs.description: Extra classes merged onto the `block` host, which is the element actually animated — the projected content moves with it.

inputs.name: delay
inputs.description: Milliseconds to wait before the reveal begins, counted from the moment it is triggered. Give siblings increasing values to stagger a group by hand.

inputs.name: direction
inputs.description: Direction the content travels *towards* over a fixed 8px: `'up'` starts 8px low and rises. Physical, not logical — it does not flip in RTL.

inputs.name: duration
inputs.description: Length of the fade/blur/slide in milliseconds. Skipped entirely when the user prefers reduced motion — the content is then shown immediately at full opacity.

inputs.name: inView
inputs.description: When true (the default) the reveal waits until the host is ~10% visible in the viewport, then fires once and stops observing. Set it to `false` to play immediately on init instead — useful inside an already-visible container or a modal.

outputs.name: replay
outputs.description: Emitted whenever {@link playAnimation} restarts a reveal that has already run once. The first reveal — automatic or manual — is not a replay and stays silent, so a counter bound here reports repeats only.

inputs.name: boxRadius
inputs.description: Corner rounding of each box rect, in px (SVG `rx`). Use `0` for square corners.

inputs.name: class
inputs.description: Extra classes merged onto the chart container, which already carries `relative w-full`.

inputs.name: dir
inputs.description: Layout direction. `'auto'` (default) resolves from the host element's inherited DOM direction after view init; `'ltr'`/`'rtl'` force it. RTL mirrors the *category* axis — the first group on the right in vertical orientation, the value axis right-to-left in horizontal. See {@link isRtl}.

inputs.name: groups
inputs.description: One box per entry, drawn in array order. Each group supplies **either** a raw `values` sample — summarised here — **or** a pre-computed `stats`, which wins when both are present; the two paths lay out identically. Groups carrying neither (or an empty `values`) are skipped rather than drawn as a degenerate box, so a chart whose groups are all unusable falls back to the empty state.

inputs.name: height
inputs.description: Height of the SVG in px, applied literally.

inputs.name: orientation
inputs.description: `'vertical'` (default) runs the category axis across the width and the value axis up the height; `'horizontal'` transposes both, which reads better for long category labels.

inputs.name: showGrid
inputs.description: Draw the dashed gridline behind each value tick. The tick *labels* are drawn either way.

inputs.name: showOutliers
inputs.description: Draw the samples beyond the 1.5×IQR fences as individual focusable points. The whiskers are unaffected — they always stop at the fence.

inputs.name: showTooltip
inputs.description: Show the shared tooltip listing the five-number summary. Hover still emits {@link groupHover} when disabled.

inputs.name: title
inputs.description: Human-readable chart name, used only to prefix the container's accessible summary ("<title>. Box plot with N data points.").

inputs.name: unit
inputs.description: Suffix appended to every rendered number — tooltip, tick labels and aria-labels alike (e.g. `'ms'`, `'°C'`). Written verbatim with no separating space.

inputs.name: width
inputs.description: Fallback width of the SVG user-space coordinate system, in px, used until the host has been measured — from then on the `viewBox` tracks the host's real width. The measurement needs a block-level box, which is why the host is `class: 'block'` and the container `w-full`.

outputs.name: groupClick
outputs.description: Emitted when a box is clicked, or activated with Enter/Space while focused. `point` is the original {@link BoxplotGroup}.

outputs.name: groupHover
outputs.description: Emitted with the group on hover/focus and with `null` on mouse-leave/blur, so consumers can mirror the highlight.

inputs.name: locale
inputs.description: Locale dictionary or registry key. Falls back to `UI_LOCALE_ID` when not set.

inputs.name: class
inputs.description: Extra classes merged onto the ellipsis marker. The dots are decorative (`aria-hidden`); a localized "more" label is exposed to screen readers behind them.

inputs.name: locale
inputs.description: Locale dictionary or registry key. Falls back to `UI_LOCALE_ID` (which is broadcast by the parent `<ui-breadcrumb>`).

inputs.name: class
inputs.description: Extra classes merged onto the item host, which lays a link plus any adornment (icon, badge) out in a row. Separators are siblings of the item, not children.

inputs.name: class
inputs.description: Extra classes merged onto the anchor. Colour comes from the list (`text-muted-foreground`); only the hover state is set here.

inputs.name: href
inputs.description: Destination of the crumb, set on a plain `<a href>`. Defaults to `'#'`, so a link left unset navigates nowhere rather than breaking. For client-side routing, project a `routerLink` anchor instead of using this component.

inputs.name: class
inputs.description: Extra classes merged onto the list. It already wraps onto multiple lines and tightens its gap below the `sm` breakpoint, so deep trails degrade gracefully on phones.

inputs.name: items
inputs.description: Data-driven mode: the whole trail as an array, with separators inserted automatically and the entry flagged `isCurrentPage` rendered as the non-clickable end of the trail. A non-empty array takes priority over any projected content, which is then ignored entirely.

inputs.name: skeleton
inputs.description: Renders {@link skeletonCount} placeholder crumbs instead of the real trail. Outranks both {@link items} and projected content while set.

inputs.name: skeletonCount
inputs.description: How many placeholder crumbs the skeleton shows — pick the depth you expect so the layout does not jump when the real trail arrives.

inputs.name: class
inputs.description: Extra classes merged onto the current-page crumb. It renders as a disabled `role="link"` carrying `aria-current="page"` — the trail's endpoint, deliberately not clickable.

inputs.name: class
inputs.description: Extra classes merged onto the separator host. Any projected content replaces the default chevron; the built-in `[&>svg]:size-3.5` rule sizes a custom icon to match.

inputs.name: class
inputs.description: Extra classes merged onto the chart container, which already carries `relative w-full`.

inputs.name: dir
inputs.description: Layout direction. `'auto'` (default) resolves from the host element's inherited DOM direction once, after view init; `'ltr'`/`'rtl'` force it. RTL reverses the x scale's pixel range and moves the y tick labels to the right-hand edge. See {@link isRtl}.

inputs.name: height
inputs.description: Height in px, applied verbatim to the SVG's `height` attribute and its `viewBox`, so — unlike {@link width} — it is never measured or scaled. The plot area is this minus 16px of top and 28px of bottom padding.

inputs.name: maxRadius
inputs.description: Radius in px given to the largest `z`. Radii interpolate by the square root of the normalized `z`, so bubble *area* — not diameter — is proportional to magnitude, which is what readers judge. Bubbles are not de-overlapped, so a wide {@link minRadius}–`maxRadius` span on clustered points will occlude; the plot area does not grow to accommodate it.

inputs.name: minRadius
inputs.description: Radius in px given to the smallest `z` in the data. Raise it so low-magnitude bubbles stay clickable.

inputs.name: series
inputs.description: One cloud of bubbles per series. Every `points` entry needs numeric `x` and `y` (continuous position) plus `z`, the magnitude mapped to the bubble radius between {@link minRadius} and {@link maxRadius}. All three domains are derived from the *visible* points, so hiding a series through the legend rescales the axes **and** re-sizes every remaining bubble. `color` overrides the palette colour otherwise derived from the series index, and `id` (falling back to `name`) is the legend toggle key.

inputs.name: showGrid
inputs.description: Draw the dashed horizontal gridlines behind the bubbles, one per y tick. There are no vertical gridlines.

inputs.name: showLegend
inputs.description: Render the legend under the chart. It is interactive: clicking an entry calls {@link toggleSeries}, which rescales the axes and the radius scale.

inputs.name: showTooltip
inputs.description: Show the floating tooltip (series name plus the point's x, y and z) for the bubble nearest the pointer.

inputs.name: title
inputs.description: Human-readable chart name, used only to prefix the container's accessible summary.

inputs.name: width
inputs.description: Design width of the SVG user-space coordinate system, in px, used as the `viewBox` width until the host has been measured. The rendered `<svg>` is `width="100%"`, so the chart tracks its container and this value only fixes the initial/fallback coordinate space. The container must be a block-level box — an inline-block parent collapses a `width:100%` SVG, which is why the host is `block` and the container carries `w-full`.

outputs.name: pointClick
outputs.description: Emitted when a bubble is clicked or activated with Enter while focused. `index` is the point's position **within its own series**, not a flat index across the chart, and the payload carries no series identifier — track the series yourself if you need it. The originating event is not forwarded.

inputs.name: class
inputs.description: Extra classes merged onto the `block w-full` host. Keep it full-width, since that is what the resize observer measures to size the SVG.

inputs.name: color
inputs.description: Colour of the measure bar. Defaults to the theme's primary colour; the range bands are always neutral shading and ignore this.

inputs.name: dir
inputs.description: Text direction for the labels: `'auto'` inherits from the document. The bar itself always grows left-to-right and does not mirror in RTL.

inputs.name: height
inputs.description: Height of the SVG in pixels. The measure bar takes a third of it, centred, with the range bands behind at full height. Fixed, not responsive.

inputs.name: label
inputs.description: Name of the metric, shown beside the chart and folded into the accessible label.

inputs.name: min
inputs.description: Start of the axis. The upper bound is not an input: it is derived from the largest of {@link value}, {@link target} and {@link ranges}.

inputs.name: ranges
inputs.description: Qualitative band boundaries (e.g. `[40, 70, 100]` for poor/ok/good), given as upper bounds. Bands are drawn from {@link min} up through each bound in ascending order — the list is sorted internally — with progressively stronger shading.

inputs.name: target
inputs.description: Goal marker drawn as a vertical tick across the bar. Omit it for a bar with no target line; when set it is also announced in the accessible label.

inputs.name: title
inputs.description: Chart title, prefixed to the accessible label. Supply it when the chart has no visible heading beside it.

inputs.name: unit
inputs.description: Unit suffix appended to the displayed value and to the accessible label. Cosmetic only — it does not affect the scale.

inputs.name: value
inputs.description: The measure — the primary quantity drawn as the central bar. It also participates in the auto-scale, so a value beyond every range simply extends the axis.

inputs.name: width
inputs.description: Fallback width in pixels, used only until the container has been measured — the chart normally stretches to its container's width via a resize observer.

classes.name: ButtonGroupComponent
classes.description: ButtonGroup - Group buttons together with seamless borders Usage: <ui-button-group> <ui-button variant="outline">Left</ui-button> <ui-button variant="outline">Center</ui-button> <ui-button variant="outline">Right</ui-button> </ui-button-group> <ui-button-group orientation="vertical"> <ui-button>Top</ui-button> <ui-button>Bottom</ui-button> </ui-button-group>

inputs.name: class
inputs.description: Extra classes merged onto the group wrapper — e.g. `w-full` to stretch it, since the group is `w-fit` by default.

inputs.name: orientation
inputs.description: Stacking axis. Drives which corner radii and adjoining borders are stripped from the children so they read as one control: the horizontal form uses logical `-s`/`-e` sides and therefore flips correctly in RTL. Set the matching `orientation` on any {@link ButtonGroupSeparatorComponent} inside.

classes.name: ButtonGroupSeparatorComponent
classes.description: ButtonGroupSeparator - Visual separator within a button group

inputs.name: class
inputs.description: Extra classes merged onto the rule — override `bg-border` here for a stronger or coloured divider.

inputs.name: orientation
inputs.description: Orientation of the rule itself, not of the group: `'vertical'` (the default) is a 1px-wide column for a horizontal button group, `'horizontal'` a 1px-tall row for a vertical one. It stretches to the group's cross-axis size via `self-stretch`.

classes.name: ButtonGroupTextComponent
classes.description: ButtonGroupText - Static text element within a button group Usage: <ui-button-group> <ui-button-group-text>https://</ui-button-group-text> <ui-input /> <ui-button-group-text>.com</ui-button-group-text> </ui-button-group>

inputs.name: class
inputs.description: Extra classes merged onto the text chip. The defaults already size any unstyled projected `<svg>` to `size-4` and make it click-through, so icons need no extra markup.

inputs.name: ariaLabel
inputs.description: Accessible name, camelCase form: `[ariaLabel]="'Copy'"`.

inputs.name: class
inputs.description: Extra classes merged onto the inner `<button>` (not the host).

inputs.name: disabled
inputs.description: Disables the inner `<button>`. Also forced while {@link loading} is true.

inputs.name: label
inputs.description: Convenience text label. When set it replaces projected content — pass either this or `<ng-content>`, not both.

inputs.name: loading
inputs.description: Show a centred spinner over the button's content and disable it. The label stays in the DOM, so the button keeps its width and the layout doesn't jump.

inputs.name: ripple
inputs.description: Enable the material-style ripple on press.

inputs.name: rippleColor
inputs.description: Ripple colour, any CSS colour. Defaults to a translucent tint of the current text colour.

inputs.name: size
inputs.description: Size preset. The three `icon*` sizes drop the horizontal padding for a square button holding a single glyph.

inputs.name: skeleton
inputs.description: Replace the button entirely with a skeleton placeholder while content loads.

inputs.name: type
inputs.description: Native `type` of the inner `<button>`. Defaults to `'button'` so it never submits a form by accident.

inputs.name: variant
inputs.description: Visual style. `link` renders as inline text; `destructive` is tinted, not solid.

outputs.name: clicked
outputs.description: Emits the native click. Never fires while disabled, loading, or in skeleton mode.

outputs.name: cancelled
outputs.description: Emits on every non-accepting close — the Cancel button, Escape, or a backdrop dismiss — so a caller can rely on exactly one of {@link confirmed} / {@link cancelled} firing per open.

outputs.name: confirmed
outputs.description: Emits when the user accepts. Always followed by the dialog closing.

inputs.name: cancelLabel
inputs.description: Cancel button text. Defaults to the locale's "Cancel".

inputs.name: confirmLabel
inputs.description: Confirm button text. Defaults to the locale's "Confirm".

inputs.name: confirmTitle
inputs.description: Dialog heading. Defaults to the locale's "Confirm".

inputs.name: locale
inputs.description: Locale for the default dialog strings: a registry key (`'en'`/`'he'`/…) or a full dictionary.

inputs.name: uiConfirm
inputs.description: The confirmation prompt, and the directive's own selector — applying `uiConfirm="Delete this file?"` is what enables the guard. The text becomes the dialog's description; an empty value shows title only.

outputs.name: confirmed
outputs.description: Emits only after the user confirms. The host's own click is stopped, so this — not `(click)` — is where the guarded action belongs.

inputs.name: cellSize
inputs.description: Edge of each square day cell, in px of SVG user space; cells are laid out with a fixed 3px gap. This is a design size, not a responsive one — the grid's intrinsic width grows with the number of weeks ({@link usedWidth}) and the whole SVG is then scaled down by `max-w-full` if the container is narrower, so raising it makes a long range overflow-and-shrink sooner.

inputs.name: class
inputs.description: Extra classes merged onto the container, which already carries `relative w-fit max-w-full mr-auto`.

inputs.name: data
inputs.description: One entry per day that has data. `date` must be a `YYYY-MM-DD` string — it is split on `-` and read as **UTC**, so no timezone shifting occurs and any other format (ISO datetime, `MM/DD/YYYY`, `Date`) will place the cell wrong or not at all. Grid position is derived, not given: the row is the UTC weekday (Sunday on top) and the column is the whole-week offset from the Sunday on or before the earliest date in the array, so order within the array is irrelevant and days you omit stay blank rather than being filled in. `value` drives the colour ramp across the array's own min/max (see {@link valueDomain}).

inputs.name: dir
inputs.description: Accepted for API parity with the cartesian charts, but the calendar does not read it: weeks always run in the writing direction inherited from the DOM. Wrap the host in `dir="rtl"` to flip it.

inputs.name: emptyColor
inputs.description: Intended fill for days with no data. Currently inert: only the days present in {@link data} are drawn at all, so there is no empty cell to paint — a gap shows the page background. Supply a zero-valued entry for a day you want rendered.

inputs.name: fromColor
inputs.description: Colour of the lowest value in {@link valueDomain}. Must be an `hsl(h, s%, l%)` string — {@link sequentialColorScale} parses and interpolates the H/S/L channels, so hex/rgb/`var(--…)` values will not interpolate.

inputs.name: showLegend
inputs.description: Show the Less→More strip of five swatches under the grid, sampled at even steps across {@link valueDomain}.

inputs.name: showTooltip
inputs.description: Render the floating tooltip for the hovered/focused day. Hover still emits {@link dayHover} when disabled.

inputs.name: title
inputs.description: Human-readable chart name; used only to prefix the group's accessible summary ({@link ariaLabel}).

inputs.name: toColor
inputs.description: Colour of the highest value in {@link valueDomain}; same `hsl(...)` requirement as {@link fromColor}.

outputs.name: dayHover
outputs.description: Emits the day on hover/focus and `null` on mouse-leave/blur, so a consumer can mirror the highlight elsewhere.

inputs.name: class
inputs.description: Extra classes merged onto the calendar's bordered container (`p-3 … inline-block`).

inputs.name: locale
inputs.description: Locale id or inline {@link CalendarLocale} overrides for day/month names and control labels.

inputs.name: mode
inputs.description: Selection behaviour, which also dictates the shape carried by {@link selected}: `'single'` → `Date`, `'range'` → {@link DateRange}, `'multi'` → `Date[]`. Changing it at runtime does not convert an already-set value, so reset {@link selected} alongside it.

inputs.name: rtl
inputs.description: Mirrors the direction of the arrow icons. Set automatically from the active {@link locale} whenever that locale declares `rtl`, so an explicit binding is overwritten on locale change.

inputs.name: selected
inputs.type: Date | DateRange | Date[] | string | string[] | null
inputs.description: Two-way selection. Accepts `Date`s, `'YYYY-MM-DD'` strings, or arrays of either on the way in; always emits parsed `Date`s (or a {@link DateRange}) on the way out. The first non-null value also scrolls the calendar to that month — later changes do not move the view.

inputs.name: selectedTimeRange
inputs.description: Two-way `HH:mm` pair backing the `timeMode: 'range'` footer. Acts as the time-of-day applied to days picked afterwards; days already in {@link selected} keep the time they were stored with.

inputs.name: showMonthSelect
inputs.description: Replaces the static month caption with a `ui-select` month picker. Off by default.

inputs.name: showTimeSelect
inputs.description: Renders the `<input type="time">` footer below the day grid; see {@link timeMode}.

inputs.name: showYearSelect
inputs.description: Replaces the static year caption with a `ui-select` year picker listing the current year back 100 years — years beyond that range are unreachable from the UI (navigate with {@link previousMonth} or set {@link selected} instead).

inputs.name: timeMode
inputs.description: Shape of the time footer when {@link showTimeSelect} is on: `'single'` shows one time field bound to {@link updateTime}, `'range'` shows start/end fields whose values are mirrored into {@link selectedTimeRange}. Ignored while {@link showTimeSelect} is `false`.

inputs.name: weekStartsOn
inputs.description: First column of the week as a `Date.getDay()` index — `0` = Sunday (default), `1` = Monday, … `6` = Saturday. Rotates both the weekday header and the leading blank cells of the grid.

outputs.name: rtl
outputs.description: Mirrors the direction of the arrow icons. Set automatically from the active {@link locale} whenever that locale declares `rtl`, so an explicit binding is overwritten on locale change.

outputs.name: selected
outputs.type: Date | DateRange | Date[] | string | string[] | null
outputs.description: Two-way selection. Accepts `Date`s, `'YYYY-MM-DD'` strings, or arrays of either on the way in; always emits parsed `Date`s (or a {@link DateRange}) on the way out. The first non-null value also scrolls the calendar to that month — later changes do not move the view.

outputs.name: selectedTimeRange
outputs.description: Two-way `HH:mm` pair backing the `timeMode: 'range'` footer. Acts as the time-of-day applied to days picked afterwards; days already in {@link selected} keep the time they were stored with.

inputs.name: axisMode
inputs.description: `'ordinal'` (default) gives every period present in the data an equal band, so weekends and holidays leave no blank space — what finance users expect. `'time'` places candles on a real time scale, which is correct for genuinely continuous data and does show those gaps.

inputs.name: class
inputs.description: Extra classes merged onto the chart container, which already carries `relative w-full`.

inputs.name: dir
inputs.description: Layout direction. `'auto'` (default) resolves from the host element's inherited DOM direction after view init; `'ltr'`/`'rtl'` force it. RTL reverses the period axis (the newest candle on the left) and moves the price tick labels to the opposite edge. See {@link isRtl}.

inputs.name: fallingColor
inputs.description: Colour of a candle that closed below its open. Any CSS colour, so a theme token such as `var(--destructive)` works.

inputs.name: height
inputs.description: Height of the SVG in px, applied literally.

inputs.name: locale
inputs.description: BCP-47 locale used to format `Date`/epoch-ms period labels. Ignored for label-string periods, which are printed verbatim.

inputs.name: points
inputs.description: One candle per OHLC period, drawn in array order — the series is **not** sorted, so pass it chronologically. Rows whose four prices are not all finite are dropped rather than rendered. On the default `'ordinal'` axis a period's `date` may be a plain label string; on `'time'` it must be a `Date`, epoch-ms number or parseable date string, and unplaceable rows are dropped.

inputs.name: risingColor
inputs.description: Colour of a candle that closed at or above its open. Any CSS colour, so a theme token such as `var(--chart-2)` works.

inputs.name: showGrid
inputs.description: Draw the dashed horizontal gridline behind each price tick. The tick *labels* are drawn either way.

inputs.name: showTooltip
inputs.description: Show the shared tooltip listing open/high/low/close. Hover still emits {@link candleHover} when disabled.

inputs.name: title
inputs.description: Human-readable chart name, used only to prefix the container's accessible summary ("<title>. Candlestick chart with N data points.").

inputs.name: unit
inputs.description: Suffix appended to every rendered price — tooltip, tick labels and aria-labels alike (e.g. `'$'`, `' USD'`). Written verbatim with no separating space.

inputs.name: width
inputs.description: Fallback width of the SVG user-space coordinate system, in px, used until the host has been measured — from then on the `viewBox` tracks the host's real width. The measurement needs a block-level box, which is why the host is `class: 'block'` and the container `w-full`.

outputs.name: candleClick
outputs.description: Emitted when a candle is clicked, or activated with Enter/Space while focused. `point` is the original {@link OhlcPoint}.

outputs.name: candleHover
outputs.description: Emitted with the period on hover/focus and with `null` on mouse-leave/blur, so consumers can mirror the highlight.

classes.name: CardAccordionComponent
classes.description: Card-styled accordion. Reuses the base accordion state engine (single/multiple open, collapsible, default-open) while rendering each panel as an elevated card with a smooth grid-rows height animation.

inputs.name: class
inputs.description: Extra classes merged onto the accordion wrapper, after the base `w-full`. Item borders come from `<ui-accordion-item>`, not here.

inputs.name: collapsible
inputs.description: Whether clicking the open item in `'single'` mode closes it, leaving nothing open. Defaults to `true`; set `false` to force one item to always stay open. Ignored when {@link type} is `'multiple'`, where items always toggle closed.

inputs.name: openValues
inputs.description: Values of the items to open. Applied whenever the array *reference* changes, overwriting whatever the user had open — pass a new array to drive the accordion, and leave it `null` (the default) for uncontrolled use. It is not two-way: user toggles via {@link toggle} are not written back here.

inputs.name: type
inputs.description: `'single'` (default) keeps at most one item open — opening one closes the rest; `'multiple'` lets any number stay open and makes {@link collapsible} irrelevant. Also reinterprets {@link openValues}: in `'single'` only its first entry is honoured.

classes.name: CardAccordionActionsComponent
classes.description: Header action slot (custom mode). Rendered beside the chevron, outside the toggle button, so action clicks never toggle the panel. Intended to hold `ui-button` controls.

inputs.name: class
inputs.description: Extra classes merged onto the action row. It sits outside the toggle button, so buttons projected here stay independently focusable.

classes.name: CardAccordionContentComponent
classes.description: Animated card body (custom mode). Always rendered so the grid-rows `0fr -> 1fr` transition can animate the panel height smoothly; closed content is made `inert` to keep it out of the tab order and accessibility tree.

inputs.name: class
inputs.description: Extra classes merged onto the animating grid wrapper. Padding belongs on the content you project, not here — the wrapper's height collapses to zero when closed, and padding on it would leak a sliver of the closed panel.

classes.name: CardAccordionItemComponent
classes.description: A single card panel. Supports simple mode (title/description/content inputs) and custom mode (projected trigger/actions/content).

inputs.name: class
inputs.description: Extra classes merged onto the card surface. The card already gains a deeper shadow while open, so override `shadow-sm`/`shadow-md` together if you restyle it.

inputs.name: content
inputs.description: Simple mode: body text.

inputs.name: description
inputs.description: Simple mode: optional muted subtitle under the title.

inputs.name: skeleton
inputs.description: Renders skeleton placeholders in place of the header and body, keeping the card's shape while data loads. The panel is still togglable.

inputs.name: title
inputs.description: Simple mode: header title text.

inputs.name: value
inputs.description: Unique identifier shared with the parent accordion's open-state map.

classes.name: CardAccordionTriggerComponent
classes.description: Clickable card header (custom mode). Projected title content sits on the start side; the chevron rotates on open. Action controls are projected via `ui-card-accordion-actions` and rendered outside the toggle button so their clicks never toggle the panel.

inputs.name: class
inputs.description: Extra classes merged onto the header button. It is `flex-1 min-w-0`, so long titles truncate rather than pushing the chevron and actions off the card.

inputs.name: class
inputs.description: Extra classes merged onto the card surface. Padding comes from the card's density CSS rather than inline utilities, so prefer a density variable over hard-coded `p-*` here.

inputs.name: content
inputs.description: Simple-mode body text. Plain text only and, like {@link description}, only rendered when {@link title} is set — project `ui-card-content` for rich bodies.

inputs.name: description
inputs.description: Simple-mode muted subtitle under the title. Only rendered when {@link title} is also set.

inputs.name: loading
inputs.description: Overlays a translucent scrim and a spinner across the card while keeping the content visible underneath, for in-place refreshes. Use {@link skeleton} instead for a first load with no content yet.

inputs.name: skeleton
inputs.description: Replaces the whole card with a fixed-height placeholder block, and strips the card's own surface styling. Takes precedence over every other input, including {@link loading}.

inputs.name: title
inputs.description: Simple-mode heading. Supplying it switches the card to the generated layout — header, optional {@link description} and {@link content}, then any projected content underneath. Leave it empty to compose `ui-card-header` and friends yourself.

inputs.name: class
inputs.description: Extra classes merged onto the body. It contributes no utilities of its own — spacing comes from the card's density CSS keyed on `data-slot="card-content"`.

inputs.name: class
inputs.description: Extra classes merged onto the muted subtitle. Belongs inside `ui-card-header`, where the header grid places it on the row below the title.

inputs.name: class
inputs.description: Extra classes merged onto the footer row. Add `border-t` to get a divider — the built-in `[.border-t]:pt-6` rule then supplies the matching top padding.

inputs.name: class
inputs.description: Extra classes merged onto the header grid. It reflows to two columns automatically when a `data-slot="card-action"` element is present, and adding `border-b` also adds the matching bottom padding.

inputs.name: class
inputs.description: Extra classes merged onto the title. Renders as a styled `<div>`, not a heading element — project your own `<h2>`/`<h3>` inside if the card must appear in the document outline.

inputs.name: class
inputs.description: Extra classes merged onto the `relative` root. Keep it positioned — the previous/next buttons are absolutely placed against it, and on desktop they sit just outside its edges.

inputs.name: orientation
inputs.description: Scroll axis. Also decides which arrow keys page the carousel and where the previous/next buttons are placed (sides when horizontal, above and below — rotated — when vertical). The horizontal form is RTL-aware: direction is detected from the document and the buttons swap behaviour accordingly.

inputs.name: class
inputs.description: Extra classes merged onto the scrolling track. It is the element that actually scrolls (with hidden scrollbars and mandatory snapping), and it carries a negative start margin that cancels the slides' gutter — so change `-ms-4`/`-mt-4` and the slides' padding together.

inputs.name: class
inputs.description: Extra classes merged onto the slide. It is `basis-full` — one slide per view — so override the basis to show several at once (e.g. `basis-1/2 lg:basis-1/3`). The `ps-4`/`pt-4` gutter pairs with the track's negative margin, so keep it when restyling.

inputs.name: class
inputs.description: Extra classes merged onto the button. Its position is orientation-dependent (inset on mobile, outside the carousel from `sm` up), so override the inset utilities as a set.

inputs.name: locale
inputs.description: Locale dictionary or registry key. Falls back to `UI_LOCALE_ID` when not set.

inputs.name: class
inputs.description: Extra classes merged onto the button. Its position is orientation-dependent (inset on mobile, outside the carousel from `sm` up), so override the inset utilities as a set.

inputs.name: locale
inputs.description: Locale dictionary or registry key. Falls back to `UI_LOCALE_ID` when not set.

classes.name: ChartBrushComponent
classes.description: Controlled zoom/pan/brush overlay for dense cartesian charts. Works in pixel space along the x-axis; the host chart maps pixels↔domain via a scale. Selection logic is unit-tested directly; DOM handlers (mouse + touch) just translate events to a local x and delegate to those methods.

inputs.name: class
inputs.description: Extra classes merged onto the SVG, which already carries `block w-full select-none`.

inputs.name: height
inputs.description: Rendered height of the brush strip, in px, used for both the `height` attribute and the viewBox, so it is a literal size and does not scale with the container. It also fixes the hit height of the track and of the two drag handles.

inputs.name: selection
inputs.description: Initial/controlled selection in the same pixel space as {@link width}; `null` means nothing brushed. It seeds {@link current} only until the first interaction — once the user drags, the component's internal state takes over and later changes to this input no longer move the brush. Call {@link reset} to hand control back.

inputs.name: width
inputs.description: Width of the SVG user-space coordinate system, in px, and simultaneously the clamp ceiling for every selection coordinate (`0…width`). Set it to the *plot* width of the chart being brushed so a `start`/`end` can be fed straight into that chart's x-scale `invert()` with no rescaling. The SVG itself is `w-full` with `preserveAspectRatio="none"`, so it stretches to the container regardless — this value is the domain, not the render size.

outputs.name: selectionChange
outputs.description: Fires on every pointer move during a drag (live filtering of the host chart), again on release, and with `null` when the Reset button calls {@link reset}. The payload is always normalized so `start <= end`, even while dragging leftwards.

classes.name: ChartLegendComponent
classes.description: Shared chart legend. Presentational: the host chart owns the set of hidden series keys and updates it in response to `itemToggle`. Supports keyboard and touch activation (tap = click, no hover dependency).

inputs.name: class
inputs.description: Extra classes merged onto the legend container — e.g. `text-xs` to shrink it, or extra gap utilities for denser charts.

inputs.name: hidden
inputs.description: Keys of the currently hidden series, which render dimmed. The legend is purely presentational — it never mutates this list, so the host chart must update it in response to {@link itemToggle} or nothing visibly changes.

inputs.name: interactive
inputs.description: Allows clicking, tapping or pressing Enter/Space on an entry to emit {@link itemToggle}. Set to `false` for a read-only key.

inputs.name: items
inputs.description: Series entries to list, in display order. Each `key` is the identifier echoed back by {@link itemToggle} and matched against {@link hidden}; `color` paints the swatch.

inputs.name: position
inputs.description: Where the legend sits relative to the plot. `'left'`/`'right'` stack the entries in a column; `'top'`/`'bottom'` lay them out in a wrapping row.

outputs.name: itemToggle
outputs.description: Emitted with the `key` of the activated entry when {@link interactive} is set. It signals intent only — the host decides whether to add or remove the key from {@link hidden}.

classes.name: ChartTooltipComponent
classes.description: Shared positioned tooltip for charts. Reproduces the popover styling the charts previously duplicated inline, and adds viewport-overflow protection.

inputs.name: class
inputs.description: Extra classes merged onto the tooltip surface. Keep `max-w-[calc(100vw-2rem)]` in place — it is what stops the tooltip overflowing the viewport on narrow screens.

inputs.name: flipX
inputs.description: Flip left of the anchor when the anchor is near the right edge.

inputs.name: flipY
inputs.description: Flip above the anchor when the anchor is near the bottom edge.

inputs.name: rows
inputs.description: Series entries listed under the title. Each row's optional `color` renders a swatch matching the series; rows without one show label and value only. `value` is taken as already formatted — no number formatting happens here.

inputs.name: title
inputs.description: Optional heading above the rows — typically the hovered category or x-axis value. Omit it for a rows-only tooltip.

inputs.name: visible
inputs.description: Shows or hides the tooltip. Hidden means not rendered at all, so there is no stale content left behind between hovers.

inputs.name: x
inputs.description: Horizontal offset in pixels from the positioned ancestor's origin — normally the chart's own `relative` wrapper, not the page. Combine with {@link flipX} near the right edge.

inputs.name: y
inputs.description: Vertical offset in pixels from the positioned ancestor's origin. Combine with {@link flipY} near the bottom edge.

inputs.name: avatarFallback
inputs.description: Initials shown when there is no usable {@link avatarSrc}. Keep it to one or two characters; the avatar is small.

inputs.name: avatarSrc
inputs.description: Avatar image URL. When it fails to load — or is omitted — {@link avatarFallback} shows instead. Not rendered at all for `'system'` messages.

inputs.name: class
inputs.description: Extra classes merged onto the message row (the flex line holding avatar and bubble), not onto the bubble itself.

inputs.name: content
inputs.description: Message text for simple mode. Ignored once anything is projected into the bubble, which is how you render markdown, tool calls or attachments instead.

inputs.name: role
inputs.description: Who sent the message. Drives the whole layout: `'user'` aligns to the end with a primary-coloured bubble and the avatar last, `'assistant'` aligns to the start, `'system'` renders as centred italic meta text with no avatar. This is a domain concept, not an ARIA role — the attribute is deliberately stripped from the DOM.

inputs.name: class
inputs.description: Extra classes merged onto the composer wrapper. It is `relative` because the send button is absolutely positioned in its bottom-end corner.

inputs.name: disabled
inputs.description: Blocks sending: the button is disabled and both Enter and {@link onSubmit} become no-ops. The textarea itself stays editable, so a half-typed message survives.

inputs.name: placeholder
inputs.description: Placeholder text in the textarea. Not localized by the component — pass a translated string.

outputs.name: send
outputs.description: Emitted with the message text when the user sends. The textarea is cleared immediately, optimistically — nothing waits for the consumer, so failed sends must be restored by the consumer.

inputs.name: autoScroll
inputs.description: Keeps the list pinned to the newest message: a `MutationObserver` watches the projected content and scrolls to the bottom on any change, including text edits (so a streaming reply keeps following). It scrolls unconditionally, so a user who has scrolled up will be yanked back down.

inputs.name: class
inputs.description: Extra classes merged onto the scroll viewport. The host is already a flex child that fills and clips, so overriding the height here is rarely needed.

inputs.name: ariaDescribedby
inputs.description: `aria-describedby` for the native input, e.g. pointing at a hint or error message.

inputs.name: ariaInvalid
inputs.description: `aria-invalid` for the native input; leave undefined to omit the attribute entirely.

inputs.name: ariaLabel
inputs.description: `aria-label` for the native input. Ignored when {@link label} is set, since the rendered label labels the control.

inputs.name: ariaLabelledby
inputs.description: `aria-labelledby` for the native input. Ignored when {@link label} is set — the generated label element is referenced instead.

inputs.name: checked
inputs.description: Two-way checked state. Also written by {@link writeValue} and emitted through the registered `onChange`.

inputs.name: class
inputs.description: Extra classes merged onto the visual box (not the host or the label).

inputs.name: disabled
inputs.description: Disables the checkbox. OR-ed with the state pushed by {@link setDisabledState}, so a reactive-forms `disable()` also wins even when this input stays `false`.

inputs.name: elementId
inputs.description: `id` for the native input. When {@link label} is set an auto-generated id is used instead so the label's `for` can bind.

inputs.name: indeterminate
