inputs.description: Renders the dash glyph and sets `data-state="indeterminate"`; purely visual — it does not change {@link checked}, and toggling clears it only if the consumer does.

inputs.name: label
inputs.description: Simple mode: renders an associated `<label>` next to the box, wired to the auto-generated id.

inputs.name: skeleton
inputs.description: Renders placeholder blocks instead of the control; the label slot gets its own placeholder when {@link label} is set.

outputs.name: checked
outputs.description: Two-way checked state. Also written by {@link writeValue} and emitted through the registered `onChange`.

inputs.name: allowDuplicates
inputs.description: When `false` (default), re-adding text that already exists as a chip is silently dropped and only clears the field. Set `true` to allow repeats.

inputs.name: badgeVariant
inputs.description: Badge variant used for every chip. Overridden per chip to `default` whenever {@link chipColors} supplies that chip a background.

inputs.name: chipColors
inputs.description: Per-chip background colours keyed by the exact chip text. A matched chip is forced to the `default` badge variant and painted with this background, border, and a luminance-derived foreground (see {@link chipForeground}) so light colours stay readable. Unlisted chips keep {@link badgeVariant}.

inputs.name: class
inputs.description: Merged onto the chip container (after the {@link variant} classes), so it can override the border, ring, or padding.

inputs.name: disabled
inputs.description: Disables the whole control: the field is inert, the per-chip remove buttons are removed from the DOM entirely (not just hidden), and {@link focusInput} becomes a no-op. A reactive `control.disable()` disables the control too — both sources are OR-ed together by {@link isDisabled}.

inputs.name: maxRows
inputs.description: Caps the container height at this many rows (36px each plus 8px padding) and makes it scroll instead of growing. `0` (default) means unlimited — the container grows with every added chip.

inputs.name: placeholder
inputs.description: Text shown in the inline text field, and its `aria-label`. The placeholder text itself is cleared once the first chip exists (the label stays), so it never competes visually with the chips beside it.

inputs.name: separatorKeys
inputs.description: Extra `KeyboardEvent.key` values that commit the typed text as a chip, e.g. `[',', ' ']`. Enter always commits regardless of this list; the keys are matched exactly and are consumed (`preventDefault`) so they never reach the text field.

inputs.name: variant
inputs.description: Shell styling of the chip container: bordered box (`outline`), a single bottom rule (`underline`), or no chrome at all (`ghost`). Only `outline`/`underline` render a focus ring.

outputs.name: chipAdded
outputs.description: Emits the trimmed chip text after it has been appended — not emitted for text rejected as a duplicate.

outputs.name: chipRemoved
outputs.description: Emits the removed chip's text, both for the remove button ({@link removeChip}) and for the Backspace-on-empty-field shortcut.

inputs.name: class
inputs.description: Extra classes merged onto the block. The surface is deliberately dark in both themes (`bg-zinc-950`), so override it here if you need a light code block.

inputs.name: code
inputs.description: Source text to display. Split on newlines and tokenized line by line, so highlighting never spans lines — a multi-line string or block comment is coloured per line.

inputs.name: collapseScope
inputs.description: Enables collapsible code folding on brace/indent scopes. Requires a scope detector for the resolved language — languages without one simply render flat.

inputs.name: customLanguages
inputs.description: Extra or replacement language definitions keyed by lowercase language name. A bare pattern array registers highlighting only; a full config may also supply a scope detector for folding. An entry here shadows the built-in language of the same name, but still inherits that language's built-in fold detector when it does not provide one.

inputs.name: defaultCollapsed
inputs.description: Folds every scope at this nesting depth or deeper on load (`0` collapses everything). `undefined` starts fully expanded. Only applies while {@link collapseScope} is on.

inputs.name: language
inputs.description: Language key for the highlighter, matched case-insensitively against the built-in set plus {@link customLanguages}. An unknown key silently falls back to TypeScript rules.

inputs.name: lineNumbers
inputs.description: Shows the line-number gutter, sized to the digit count of the last line so it never shifts as you scroll.

inputs.name: locale
inputs.description: Locale dictionary or registry key. Falls back to `UI_LOCALE_ID` when not set.

inputs.name: theme
inputs.description: Per-token-type class overrides. Any token type missing from the object falls back to the built-in palette, so a partial theme is fine. `null` uses the defaults throughout.

inputs.name: class
inputs.description: Extra classes for the host element. It has no base styling of its own, so this is the only source of layout for the wrapper.

inputs.name: defaultOpen
inputs.description: Opens the collapsible on first render. One-way and latching: it can only ever open, never close, so flipping it back to `false` leaves the panel open, and toggling it `true` again after the user closed it re-opens. For controlled use drive {@link show} / {@link hide} instead.

inputs.name: disabled
inputs.description: Blocks opening: {@link toggle} and {@link show} become no-ops and emit nothing. {@link hide} is deliberately not gated, so a collapsible disabled while open can still be closed programmatically. Does not dim or `aria-disable` the projected trigger — style that yourself.

outputs.name: openChange
outputs.description: Emits the new open state after {@link toggle}, {@link show} or {@link hide} changes it. Not emitted for the initial {@link defaultOpen} expansion, and `show`/`hide` emit even when the state did not actually change.

inputs.name: class
inputs.description: Extra classes merged onto the panel, after the base `overflow-hidden`. The panel is removed from the DOM while closed, so height-transition classes have nothing to animate from — use it for padding and layout instead.

inputs.name: alpha
inputs.description: Shows the alpha slider and widens the emitted hex to 8 characters when `a < 1`. A fully transparent colour keeps its alpha even with this off, so a `transparent` preset never silently becomes opaque black.

inputs.name: class
inputs.description: Extra classes merged onto the trigger button (not the popover panel). Ignored in {@link inline} mode, which renders no trigger.

inputs.name: contrastBackground
inputs.description: The colour the contrast panel compares against, i.e. slot B. Changing it while slot B is the active slot is overwritten by the next colour pick — see {@link setCompareSlot}.

inputs.name: disabled
inputs.description: Disables every control. OR-ed with the form's own disabled state ({@link setDisabledState}), so a reactive form can disable the picker without this input.

inputs.name: enableEyedropper
inputs.description: Offers the screen eyedropper. The native `EyedropperAPI` is Chromium-only; elsewhere the button falls back to sampling {@link fallbackTarget}, and is useless if that is null too.

inputs.name: enableImagePick
inputs.description: Adds the "pick from image" control. The chosen file is decoded locally — nothing is uploaded — and its dominant colours land in the extracted-palette row, with the first one selected immediately.

inputs.name: fallbackTarget
inputs.description: Element the eyedropper samples when the browser has no native `EyeDropper`. Must be same-origin, or reading its pixels taints the canvas and the pick fails.

inputs.name: formats
inputs.description: Which format tabs the panel offers. Order is respected; the first entry is the tab shown initially. Only affects the editors — the emitted value is always hex.

inputs.name: imageExtractAlgorithm
inputs.description: Quantisation strategy used by {@link enableImagePick}. `'median-cut'` gives evenly spread colours; the alternatives trade fidelity for speed on large images.

inputs.name: imageExtractCount
inputs.description: How many colours to pull out of a picked image. Higher counts cost more CPU and start returning near-duplicates.

inputs.name: inline
inputs.description: Render just the picker panel, without the built-in trigger + popover (for embedding inside another popover).

inputs.name: locale
inputs.description: Locale dictionary or registry key. Falls back to `UI_LOCALE_ID` when not set.

inputs.name: maxRecent
inputs.description: How many recents to keep. Applies to both the internal list and the array emitted through {@link recentColorsChange}, and caps what is read back from {@link storageKey}.

inputs.name: presets
inputs.description: Swatches shown in the preset row. Any CSS colour `parseColor` understands; unparseable entries are ignored on click. Picking one also pushes it into the recents.

inputs.name: recentColors
inputs.description: Controlled recents. Leave `null` (default) and the picker keeps its own list; pass an array and it becomes the single source of truth — the picker stops mutating it and only emits {@link recentColorsChange}, so you must store that back or the list never grows.

inputs.name: showContrast
inputs.description: Adds the WCAG contrast panel comparing the current colour against {@link contrastBackground}.

inputs.name: showHarmonies
inputs.description: Adds the harmony panel (readable / opposite / neighbours / trio / quartet) derived from the current colour. Off by default because it makes the popover noticeably taller.

inputs.name: showRecent
inputs.description: Show the recently-used row. Turn off where recents have nowhere to live — a picker rebuilt on every open, with no `storageKey` — since the row would then only ever echo the colour just picked while taking up space.

inputs.name: storageKey
inputs.description: `localStorage` key under which recents survive a reload. Browser-only — a no-op under SSR. Two pickers sharing a key share a list on load but do not stay in sync afterwards, since each only writes its own.

inputs.name: value
inputs.description: The colour as hex, as a two-way `model()` — the control's actual value, and what makes this component a valid Signal Forms `FormValueControl`. It tracks the canonical colour on every change, programmatic ones included, so `[(value)]` and a bound `FieldTree` cannot drift from what the picker is showing. That is deliberately *not* how {@link colorChange} behaves: that output stays silent for the initial colour and for {@link writeValue}, as it always has, so binding it back into the same state does not loop and does not dirty a form control.

outputs.name: colorChange
outputs.description: The current colour as hex, emitted on every **user-driven** change of the canonical colour. Programmatic writes stay silent: neither the initial colour nor a value pushed in through {@link writeValue} is echoed back, so binding this output into the same state the picker is written from does not loop and does not mark a form control dirty.

outputs.name: recentColorsChange
outputs.description: The next recents list, emitted only while {@link recentColors} is controlled (non-null). Uncontrolled pickers keep recents internally and stay silent here.

outputs.name: value
outputs.description: The colour as hex, as a two-way `model()` — the control's actual value, and what makes this component a valid Signal Forms `FormValueControl`. It tracks the canonical colour on every change, programmatic ones included, so `[(value)]` and a bound `FieldTree` cannot drift from what the picker is showing. That is deliberately *not* how {@link colorChange} behaves: that output stays silent for the initial colour and for {@link writeValue}, as it always has, so binding it back into the same state does not loop and does not dirty a form control.

inputs.name: barGap
inputs.description: Gap between adjacent columns, in px of user space. Column width is whatever is left of the plot area after the gaps, so raising this on a dense series narrows the columns rather than widening the chart.

inputs.name: barRadius
inputs.description: Corner rounding of each column rect, in px (SVG `rx`). Use `0` for square corners.

inputs.name: class
inputs.description: Extra classes merged onto the chart container, which already carries `relative block w-full`.

inputs.name: data
inputs.description: One floating column per entry, drawn in array order (right-to-left when {@link isRtl} resolves true). Each {@link RangeDataPoint} spans `low` to `high` rather than starting at zero — temperature bands, min/max ranges, confidence intervals — so the value axis is derived from both ends and need not include 0 (see {@link dataRange}). `name` is the category label under the axis and the optional `color` overrides the palette colour picked from the entry's index. A `low` above its `high` inverts the bar's height; it is clamped to 1px rather than flipped, so pass the ends the right way round.

inputs.name: dir
inputs.description: Layout direction. `'auto'` (default) resolves from the host element's inherited DOM direction after view init; `'ltr'`/`'rtl'` force it. RTL mirrors the column order (first entry on the right) and swaps the axis gutter to the right-hand side. See {@link isRtl}.

inputs.name: height
inputs.description: Design height of the SVG coordinate system, in px. Combined with the measured width it fixes the `aspect-ratio`, so the chart keeps its proportions while scaling — height is never measured from the DOM.

inputs.name: showGrid
inputs.description: Draw the dashed value-axis gridlines behind the columns, one per {@link axisTicks} entry.

inputs.name: showRangeLabels
inputs.description: Print the formatted `high` above each column and its `low` below (see {@link formatValue}). Turn it off for dense series where the two labels collide; the values stay reachable via the hover tooltip and the aria-label.

inputs.name: title
inputs.description: Human-readable chart name, used only to prefix the SVG's accessible summary (see {@link chartAriaLabel}).

inputs.name: unit
inputs.description: Suffix appended to every rendered number — range labels, axis ticks, tooltip and aria-labels alike (e.g. `'°C'`, `'%'`, `' mm'`). Written verbatim with no separating space, so include one yourself if the unit needs it. See {@link formatValue} and {@link formatAxisValue}.

inputs.name: width
inputs.description: Design width of the SVG user-space coordinate system, in px, and the fallback until the host element has been measured. The rendered SVG is `width="100%"` with this as its `max-width`, so the chart scales down inside narrow containers but never past this width. The host must be a block-level box — an inline-block parent collapses a `width:100%` SVG, which is why the container carries `w-full` and the host `class: 'block'`.

outputs.name: barClick
outputs.description: Emitted when a column is clicked, or activated with Enter/Space while focused. The payload's `point` is the original {@link RangeDataPoint}, low and high included.

inputs.name: barRadius
inputs.description: Corner rounding of each bar rect, in px (SVG `rx`). Use `0` for square corners; keep it small since grouped bars are narrow.

inputs.name: barSeries
inputs.description: The bar half of the chart, read against the **primary** (left) axis, which is anchored at 0 and auto-scaled to the largest value across all bar series — so negative values fall outside the plot. The **first** series is privileged: its `data[].name`s define the category axis ({@link categories}) and its values feed {@link cumulativePercents}. Further series are grouped side by side inside each category band and are indexed positionally, so every series must list its values in the same category order; a missing slot is drawn as 0.

inputs.name: class
inputs.description: Extra classes merged onto the chart container, which already carries `relative w-full`.

inputs.name: cumulativeLabel
inputs.description: Name given to the {@link showCumulative} line in the legend and its tooltip row. Ignored while `showCumulative` is false.

inputs.name: dir
inputs.description: Layout direction. `'auto'` (default) resolves from the host element's inherited DOM direction once, after view init; `'ltr'`/`'rtl'` force it. RTL reverses the category band order (and with it the bars, lines and crosshair); the primary tick labels stay on the left. See {@link isRtl}.

inputs.name: height
inputs.description: Height in px, applied verbatim to the SVG's `height` attribute and its `viewBox`, so — unlike {@link width} — it is never measured or scaled. The plot area is this minus 12px of top and 28px of bottom padding for the category labels.

inputs.name: lineSeries
inputs.description: Overlaid lines read against the **secondary** axis, whose scale is independent of the bars — that is the point of a combo chart, and the reason a line can sit above a taller bar. Points are placed at the category band centres by array position, so `data` must align with {@link barSeries}[0]. Palette colours continue after the bar series so lines never collide with bar colours. The secondary axis is drawn without tick labels, so put its unit in {@link cumulativeLabel} or the series name.

inputs.name: showCumulative
inputs.description: Prepend a Pareto-style running-total line, computed from {@link barSeries}[0] only and expressed as a percentage of that series' total. Turning it on pins the secondary axis to a fixed 0–100 range, which also rescales any {@link lineSeries} drawn alongside it.

inputs.name: showGrid
inputs.description: Draw the dashed horizontal gridlines behind the plot, one per primary-axis tick. The secondary axis contributes none.

inputs.name: showLegend
inputs.description: Render the legend (bar series, then lines) under the chart. Unlike the scatter/bubble charts this legend is non-interactive — series cannot be toggled off.

inputs.name: showTooltip
inputs.description: Show the shared tooltip for the hovered category — one row per bar series, per line series, and for the cumulative line when enabled. Disabling it keeps the crosshair and the bar dimming.

inputs.name: title
inputs.description: Human-readable chart name, used only to prefix the container's accessible summary.

inputs.name: width
inputs.description: Design width of the SVG user-space coordinate system, in px, used as the `viewBox` width until the host has been measured. The rendered `<svg>` is `width="100%"`, so the chart tracks its container and this value only fixes the initial/fallback coordinate space. The container must be a block-level box — an inline-block parent collapses a `width:100%` SVG, which is why the host is `block` and the container carries `w-full`.

outputs.name: barClick
outputs.description: Emitted when any bar is clicked. `index` is the category index and `point` the matching {@link barSeries} datum — but the template wires every rect to bar series 0, so with several bar series the payload reports the first series' value for that category regardless of which grouped bar was hit. Call {@link onBarClick} directly if you need the exact series.

inputs.name: class
inputs.description: Merged onto the palette shell (`flex h-full w-full flex-col rounded-md bg-popover`); use it to set a height or width, since the shell only fills its parent.

inputs.name: debounce
inputs.description: Milliseconds of quiet typing before {@link source} is called. `0` calls it on every keystroke.

inputs.name: recentKey
inputs.description: localStorage key for the recently-selected list. `null` (default) keeps recents in memory for the session — the developer keeps full control by reading {@link recents} and writing their own store instead.

inputs.name: recentLimit
inputs.description: How many recently-selected values to keep.

inputs.name: search
inputs.description: Controlled search text. Leave at `null` (default) to let `ui-command-input` own the query; any non-null value is pushed into the shared state on every change, overriding what the user typed.

inputs.name: shouldFilter
inputs.description: When `true` (default) items are shown only while their `value` contains the current {@link search} text, and groups with no surviving item hide too. Set `false` to take over filtering yourself — every registered item then stays visible and arrow-key navigation walks all of them.

inputs.name: source
inputs.description: Async row provider — a server-side search, typically. Leave `null` (default) and the palette stays purely projection-driven, exactly as before. When set, calls are debounced by {@link debounce} and any answer a newer keystroke has superseded is discarded, so results can never go backwards; the superseded call's `AbortSignal` is aborted too. Read the rows from {@link results} and render them as `ui-command-item`s yourself, which keeps the item API — filtering, highlight, shortcuts — unchanged. **Set `[shouldFilter]="false"` when the source already filters.** It defaults to `true`, which re-filters the rendered items client-side against the same query — so a server result whose `value` does not contain the typed text (a fuzzy match, a synonym, an id lookup) is fetched and then silently hidden. That is the usual reason an async palette "returns nothing".

inputs.name: open
inputs.description: Two-way open state of the underlying `ui-dialog`. Toggled by the global {@link shortcut}, and each transition to open focuses the projected `ui-command-input` on the next tick.

inputs.name: shortcut
inputs.description: Global key combo that toggles {@link open}, in `ShortcutBindingService` syntax — `Mod` resolves to Cmd on macOS and Ctrl elsewhere. Defaults to `Mod+K`. Registered with `scope: 'global'`, so it fires regardless of focus.

inputs.name: shortcutActionId
inputs.description: Identity of the binding in `ShortcutBindingService`, which is what a shortcut-settings UI persists user remappings against. Defaults to `command-dialog.toggle`; give each dialog instance a distinct id when a page hosts more than one, or they overwrite each other's binding.

inputs.name: shortcutCategory
inputs.description: Grouping label the binding is filed under in a shortcuts cheat-sheet or settings screen. Defaults to `Navigation`.

inputs.name: shortcutEnabled
inputs.description: Set `false` to drop the global key binding entirely (the handle is unregistered) and drive {@link open} yourself. A blank {@link shortcut} or {@link shortcutActionId} has the same effect.

outputs.name: open
outputs.description: Two-way open state of the underlying `ui-dialog`. Toggled by the global {@link shortcut}, and each transition to open focuses the projected `ui-command-input` on the next tick.

inputs.name: class
inputs.description: Merged onto the group wrapper. Note the group hides itself (via `hidden`) whenever every one of its items is filtered out, so display utilities here can be overridden.

inputs.name: heading
inputs.description: Section label rendered above the items; omit it and no heading row is emitted at all. It is not matched against the search query — only item values are.

inputs.name: ariaLabel
inputs.description: Override for the aria-label. Falls back to the locale's `search`.

inputs.name: locale
inputs.description: Locale dictionary or registry key. Falls back to `UI_LOCALE_ID` when not set.

inputs.name: placeholder
inputs.description: Override for the placeholder. Falls back to the locale's `searchPlaceholder`.

inputs.name: value
inputs.description: Seed query, applied to the shared search state once in `ngOnInit` and only when non-empty — later changes to this input are ignored. Bind `search` on the parent `ui-command` for a genuinely controlled query.

inputs.name: class
inputs.description: Merged onto the row. The keyboard-highlighted row already gets `bg-accent text-accent-foreground`, so an accent background here will fight that state.

inputs.name: disabled
inputs.description: Greys the row (50% opacity) and blocks pointer events, and suppresses {@link selectItem} on both click and Enter. It is *not* skipped by arrow-key navigation: a disabled row can still become the highlighted item, where Enter silently does nothing.

inputs.name: selected
inputs.description: Sets `aria-selected` on the row. Purely an ARIA hint for persistent selection — it is independent of the keyboard highlight and applies no styling of its own.

inputs.name: shortcut
inputs.description: Key hint rendered right-aligned on the row, e.g. `⌘P`. Display only — it binds no key handler and is not matched by the search.

inputs.name: value
inputs.description: The text filtering matches (case-insensitive substring of the query) and the payload emitted by {@link selectItem}. Read once at registration, so it must be static — and an item left with the default empty value disappears as soon as the user types anything.

outputs.name: selectItem
outputs.description: Emits {@link value} when the row is activated by click, Enter on the focused row, or Enter while it is the highlighted item. Never emits while {@link disabled}.

inputs.name: ariaLabel
inputs.description: Accessible name for the `role="listbox"` wrapper. Unset leaves it unnamed, so provide one whenever the list has no visible label near it.

inputs.name: class
inputs.description: Merged onto the scroll container; override the default `max-h-[200px] sm:max-h-[300px]` here to change how tall the results area grows before it scrolls.

inputs.name: afterAlt
inputs.description: Alt text for the after image.

inputs.name: afterLabel
inputs.description: Caption badge pinned to the top-end corner (e.g. "Edited"). Omitted entirely when unset; it truncates rather than wrapping on narrow screens.

inputs.name: afterSrc
inputs.description: Source of the "after" image, drawn underneath and revealed as the divider moves.

inputs.name: beforeAlt
inputs.description: Alt text for the before image. Leave empty only when the pair is purely decorative — the two images are separate elements to assistive tech.

inputs.name: beforeLabel
inputs.description: Caption badge pinned to the top-start corner (e.g. "Original"). Omitted entirely when unset — there is no default text.

inputs.name: beforeSrc
inputs.description: Source of the "before" image — the clipped layer on the start side of the divider. Both images should share the same dimensions, or they will not line up under the reveal.

inputs.name: class
inputs.description: Extra classes merged onto the root. It is `aspect-video` by default — override that to match your images' ratio, since both layers are absolutely positioned inside it.

inputs.name: locale
inputs.description: Locale dictionary or registry key. Falls back to `UI_LOCALE_ID` when not set.

inputs.name: orientation
inputs.description: Split axis: `'horizontal'` wipes left-to-right, `'vertical'` top-to-bottom. Also swaps which arrow keys nudge the divider.

inputs.name: position
inputs.description: Divider position as a percentage from the start edge (left, or top when vertical), 0–100. Two-way: dragging, tapping the track and the arrow keys all write back to it, and it is always clamped into range.

outputs.name: position
outputs.description: Divider position as a percentage from the start edge (left, or top when vertical), 0–100. Two-way: dragging, tapping the track and the arrow keys all write back to it, and it is always clamped into range.

classes.name: StoryAlertCardComponent
classes.description: A simple presentational component rendered dynamically by the outlet.

classes.name: StoryCompactRowComponent
classes.description: A second renderer for the same `{ title, message }` data — swapping between renderers that share an input contract is the canonical outlet use case.

classes.name: StoryOutletRecycleHostComponent
classes.description: Recycling host — rows are added / removed and instances come back from the pool.

classes.name: StoryOutletSwapHostComponent
classes.description: Interactive host for the swap / recycle stories.

classes.name: StoryStatTileComponent
classes.description: A stat tile — used for the inputs and recycling stories.

classes.name: StoryVoteCardComponent
classes.description: A component with an output, used to demonstrate the `outputs` map.

classes.name: ContextMenuAttachDirective
classes.description: Attach a context menu to any element with data. Right-clicking the host element opens the provided {@link ContextMenuComponent} at the cursor position and emits {@link ContextMenuEvent} with the bound data.

inputs.name: items
inputs.description: Data-driven menu contents. When non-empty the component renders its own `<ui-context-menu-content>` from this array (separators, labels, nested `sub` branches and items, recursively), so you only project a trigger. Leave it empty (the default) to hand-author the content with `<ui-context-menu-content>` and friends — both forms may not be combined, as a non-empty array appends a second content block after your projected one. Each entry's `click` callback fires before the menu closes; see {@link ContextMenuItem}.

inputs.name: class
inputs.description: Extra classes for the floating panel, merged after the defaults (`min-w-[8rem]`, popover colours, `max-w-[calc(100vw-16px)]` / `max-h-[calc(100vh-16px)]` scroll clamps, enter animation). The panel is portalled to `document.body` with `position: fixed` and `z-index: 9999`, so it inherits nothing from the host — width, padding and colours must be set here rather than on an ancestor. Avoid overriding `position`/`left`/ `top`: they are re-applied from the clamped coordinates on every open.

inputs.name: class
inputs.description: Extra classes merged after the defaults on the host element (the item is its own host, there is no inner wrapper).

inputs.name: disabled
inputs.description: Greys the item to 50% and sets `pointer-events: none`, so neither hover nor a click reaches it and {@link onClick} never runs. Note it emits no `aria-disabled`/`data-disabled` attribute and the item carries no `role="menuitem"`, so a disabled item is invisible to assistive tech — and no item participates in the sub-menu arrow-key ring, which only walks `[role="menuitem"]:not([data-disabled])`.

inputs.name: inset
inputs.description: Adds `ps-8` start padding so a label-less item lines up with siblings that carry a leading icon; also reflected as `data-inset` for styling.

inputs.name: shortcut
inputs.description: Accelerator hint rendered end-aligned in muted small caps (e.g. `'⌘C'`). Display only — it binds no key handler; wire the shortcut yourself.

inputs.name: variant
inputs.description: `'destructive'` paints the label and its focus/hover background in the destructive palette; reflected as `data-variant` for custom styling.

inputs.name: class
inputs.description: Extra classes merged after the defaults on the host element; use it to re-colour or re-space a section heading.

inputs.name: inset
inputs.description: Adds `ps-8` start padding so the heading aligns with inset items below it; also reflected as `data-inset`.

inputs.name: class
inputs.description: Extra classes for the flyout panel, merged after the defaults. Like the root content this is portalled to `document.body` (`position: fixed`, `z-index: 10000` so it stacks above the root menu), positioned 4px to the inline-end of its trigger — flipping to the other side, then clamping 8px inside the viewport, when it would overflow. Overriding `position`/ `left`/`top` fights that logic.

inputs.name: class
inputs.description: Extra classes for the inner trigger row, merged after the defaults (the host itself is `display: contents`, so styling the host has no effect).

inputs.name: disabled
inputs.description: Disables the branch: the value is written to `data-disabled` and `aria-disabled`, so the `data-[disabled]:` styling dims the row and makes it `pointer-events-none`, the row drops out of the arrow-key ring (which walks `[role="menuitem"]:not([data-disabled])`), and neither hover nor the keyboard opens the flyout. Accepts a bare attribute (`disabled`) via `booleanAttribute`.

inputs.name: inset
inputs.description: Adds `pl-8` (LTR) / `pr-8` (RTL) so the branch label aligns with inset siblings.

classes.name: ContextMenuTriggerDirective
classes.description:
ContextMenuTriggerDirective - Directive version for use on any element Usage: Action 1 Action 2
Right-click anywhere here

inputs.name: uiContextMenuTrigger
inputs.description: The menu instance this element opens — bind a template reference to the `<ui-context-menu>` (e.g. `[uiContextMenuTrigger]="contextMenu"`). Unlike `<ui-context-menu-trigger>`, the menu need not be an ancestor, so one menu can be shared by many triggers; pair that with `ContextMenuComponent.show`'s `data` argument to tell them apart. Required — omitting it is a compile-time error.

classes.name: DataListComponent
classes.description: Read-only label→value description list — the counterpart to `table` for detail panes, and the semantically correct answer to the two-column key/value layouts people build out of `<table>`. Dual mode, per `.claude/CLAUDE.md`: pass {@link items} for the plain case, or project `ui-data-list-item` children for arbitrary per-row content. Both may be combined — generated rows render first, projected rows after. The output is a real `<dl>` with `<dt>`/`<dd>` children (UC-13). Every wrapper between them is `display: contents` so the pairing survives to assistive tech (risk R-4).

inputs.name: class
inputs.description: Extra classes merged onto the inner `<dl>`.

inputs.name: items
inputs.description: Simple mode rows. Rendered before any projected `ui-data-list-item`.

inputs.name: orientation
inputs.description: `'vertical'` stacks each value under its label. `'horizontal'` puts labels beside values from the `sm` breakpoint up, and collapses back to stacked below it so nothing is squeezed on a phone (UC-12).

classes.name: DataListItemComponent
classes.description: One projected row of a `ui-data-list`: a plain-text label and arbitrary projected content as its value. The row's markup lives in an `<ng-template>` rather than in this component's host element, and the parent stamps it into its `<dl>` through `ngTemplateOutlet`. That is not indirection for its own sake — it is what makes the `<dt>`/`<dd>` **direct** children of the `<dl>`. The obvious alternative, projecting `<ui-data-list-item>` into the `<dl>` and giving it `display: contents`, looks right and is what risk R-4 in the spec suggests, but axe rejects it: `definition-list` and `dlitem` inspect the DOM tree, not the accessibility tree, so a custom element between `<dl>` and `<dt>` is a serious violation no matter what it computes to. Because the parent renders no `<ng-content>` inside the list, these host elements are never attached to the document at all.

inputs.name: class
inputs.description: Extra classes merged onto the `<dd>` holding the projected value.

inputs.name: label
inputs.description: The row's term. Rendered into the `<dt>`.

classes.name: DataTableContextMenuDirective
classes.description: Attach a context menu to a `<ui-data-table>` element. Right-clicking a row opens the provided {@link ContextMenuComponent} and emits {@link TableRowContextMenuEvent}. Right-clicking a header (when `contextMenuRowsOnly` is false) emits {@link DataTableHeaderContextMenuEvent}.

classes.name: DataTableRangeChartComponent
classes.description: Optional, opt-in dialog that charts a data-table range selection. Wire it to the table's `(rangeChartOpen)` output: ```html <ui-data-table (rangeChartOpen)="payload.set($event); chartOpen.set(true)" /> <ui-data-table-range-chart [payload]="payload()" [(open)]="chartOpen" /> ```

inputs.name: chartType
inputs.description: Active chart type; two-way so consumers can preset/observe it.

inputs.name: class
inputs.description: Extra classes merged onto the chart body wrapper inside the dialog (not the dialog surface itself).

inputs.name: open
inputs.description: Two-way dialog visibility.

inputs.name: payload
inputs.description: The range payload to chart; the dialog shows nothing useful when null.

inputs.name: title
inputs.description: Dialog title.

outputs.name: chartType
outputs.description: Active chart type; two-way so consumers can preset/observe it.

outputs.name: open
outputs.description: Two-way dialog visibility.

classes.name: DataTableContextMenuDirective
classes.description: Opt-in context-menu addon for `<ui-data-table>`. Attaches via DI to the `DataTableAddonHost` the base provides, contributes the ⋮ row/header buttons through the host's generic slot registries, and renders menus itself (imperative `ContextMenuComponent`) — the base ships no context-menu code or dependency. Reachable by mouse (`contextmenu`), touch (long-press), and the ⋮ buttons.

inputs.name: enableColumnMenu
inputs.description: Enable the per-column header menu (sort / pin / hide).

inputs.name: rowActions
inputs.description: Consumer callback returning the menu items for a row.

outputs.name: columnMenuOpen
outputs.description: Emitted when a column menu opens (with its column).

outputs.name: rowMenuOpen
outputs.description: Emitted when a row menu opens (with its context).

classes.name: DataTableExportDirective
classes.description: Opt-in CSV/Excel export addon for `<ui-data-table>`. Attaches via DI to the `DataTableAddonHost` the base provides, reads the current rows/columns and query through the host, and downloads the file itself — the base ships no export code and no `xlsx` dependency. Grab a template reference (`#exp="uiDtExport"`) and call `exp.exportToCsv()` / `exp.exportToExcel()`.

inputs.name: exportDataProvider
inputs.description: Server-side export hook: given the current query, returns all matching rows.

inputs.name: uiDtExportLocale
inputs.description: Locale for the busy label: a registry key (`'en'`/`'he'`) or a full dictionary.

classes.name: DataTablePivotDirective
classes.description: Opt-in pivot addon for `<ui-data-table>`. Attaches via DI to the `DataTableAddonHost` the base provides and exposes `getPivot(config)` — a pivot (rows x columns x values) of the table's raw data computed through the base's accessors. Grab a template reference (`#pv="uiDtPivot"`) and bind the result's `columns` / `rows` to another `<ui-data-table>` to render it. The base ships no pivot code; the pure `computePivot` is re-exported for callers that pivot arbitrary data without a table instance.

inputs.name: advancedFilter
inputs.description: Advanced AND/OR filter tree (A5). Applied in addition to global/column filters.

inputs.name: aiProvider
inputs.description: Bring-your-own AI hook. Enables natural-language filtering (`applyNaturalLanguageFilter`) and column AI-fill (`aiFillColumn`). Optional; no provider → those methods no-op (graceful degradation).

inputs.name: cellFlashDuration
inputs.description: Milliseconds a changed cell stays highlighted. See {@link enableCellFlash}.

inputs.name: collapsedGroups
inputs.description: Per-group collapsed state, keyed by the stringified group value.

inputs.name: columnFilters
inputs.description: Per-column filter values keyed by accessor key. A value is applied only if the column declares `enableFiltering`; it then runs the column's `filterFn`, or a case-insensitive substring match on the cell's string value. Empty values (null/''/[]) are skipped, so clearing a filter means writing one of those, not deleting the key.

inputs.name: columnOrder
inputs.description: Accessor keys in display order. Keys absent from this array keep their declaration order after the listed ones, so a partial order is legal. Pinned/sticky columns are still grouped to their side.

inputs.name: columns
inputs.description: See columnHelper for a type-safe fluent builder API

inputs.name: columnVisibility
inputs.description: Column visibility keyed by accessor key. Only `false` hides — a missing key counts as visible, so hiding requires writing `false`, not deleting.

inputs.name: columnWidths
inputs.description: Runtime column widths (CSS length strings) keyed by accessor key, overriding each column's declared `width`. Written by {@link enableColumnResize}; a good thing to persist and restore — see {@link getColumnState} / {@link applyColumnState}.

inputs.name: data
inputs.description: The row array. A `model`, and the table *does* write back to it: inline edits committed through a column `valueSetter`, fill-handle, paste and undo/redo all emit a new array here, as does a row drag while {@link localReorder} is on. Filtering, sorting and pagination never mutate it — they derive views.

inputs.name: disabledRowIds
inputs.description: Disabled rows addressed by {@link getRowId}. Accepts a `Set` (used directly) or an array (copied into a `Set`). See {@link isRowDisabled}.

inputs.name: emptyStateComponent
inputs.description: Replaces the "No results found." placeholder shown when the *filtered* row set is empty. It is not shown while {@link skeleton} or the loading overlay is up.

inputs.name: emptyStateComponentInputs
inputs.description: Inputs bound onto {@link emptyStateComponent}.

inputs.name: enableAdvancedFilter
inputs.description: Show the advanced-filter builder button in the toolbar.

inputs.name: enableCellFlash
inputs.description: Briefly highlights cells whose value changed between two {@link data} emissions — for live/streaming feeds. Requires a stable {@link getRowId}; with the default id function the table warns and skips flashing.

inputs.name: enableCellRangeSelection
inputs.description: Enables Excel-style rectangular cell-range selection by dragging across cells (also disables text selection in the grid). Prerequisite for {@link enableRangeActions} and {@link enableFillHandle}, and it widens `Ctrl/Cmd+C` to copy the whole range as TSV.

inputs.name: enableClipboardPaste
inputs.description: Allow pasting a clipboard grid (TSV/CSV) into cells starting at the focused cell (`Ctrl/Cmd+V`). Only columns with a `valueSetter` are written.

inputs.name: enableColumnReorder
inputs.description: Lets headers be dragged to reorder columns, writing the new order into the two-way {@link columnOrder}. Pinned/sticky columns keep their side regardless of order.

inputs.name: enableColumnResize
inputs.description: Adds a drag handle to each header's trailing edge (mouse and touch). Widths are stored in the two-way {@link columnWidths} map keyed by accessor key and override the column's declared width; {@link columnResize} reports each drop.

inputs.name: enableCopy
inputs.description: Enables the clipboard paths: `Ctrl/Cmd+C` and the `copy*ToClipboard` methods, all of which return early when false. The selection, expander and actions columns are never copied.

inputs.name: enableEditHistory
inputs.description: Track inline edits, fills and pastes on an undo/redo stack (`Ctrl/Cmd+Z` / `Ctrl/Cmd+Y` / `Ctrl/Cmd+Shift+Z`). Undo re-applies the inverse value through each column's `valueSetter` and re-emits `cellEdit`.

inputs.name: enableFillHandle
inputs.description: Show an Excel-style fill handle at the corner of the focused cell / range. Drag it down to fill the pattern into the rows below. Requires `enableCellRangeSelection`. Only columns with a `valueSetter` are filled.

inputs.name: enableFloatingFilters
inputs.description: Adds a second header row of per-column filter inputs. A column opts in with `enableFiltering` or a floating filter template/component; if no column does, the table warns and renders nothing. Values flow into {@link columnFilters}.

inputs.name: enableMultiSort
inputs.description: Lets shift-click stack multiple sort columns. While on, {@link sortState} is no longer authoritative — read {@link multiSortState} / {@link multiSortChange} instead.

inputs.name: enableNlFilter
inputs.description: When true (and `aiProvider` is set), the toolbar shows a natural-language filter box.

inputs.name: enableRangeActions
inputs.description: Show a contextual readout when a cell range is selected: live Sum / Avg / Count of the selection, plus a "Chart" action. Requires `enableCellRangeSelection`. Opt-in; off by default.

inputs.name: enableRowDrag
inputs.description: Makes rows draggable (HTML5 drag-and-drop). Disabled rows and rows under a {@link loading} overlay cannot be dragged.

inputs.name: enableRowExpansion
inputs.description: Adds the leading chevron column that reveals a detail row beneath each row. This is master/detail — unrelated to {@link enableSubRows}, which renders a hierarchy in the grid itself.

inputs.name: enableRowSelection
inputs.description: Adds the leading checkbox column and the header select-all checkbox.

inputs.name: enableSubRows
inputs.description: Renders hierarchical data: rows are flattened into an indented tree with expanders. Mutually exclusive with {@link groupBy}. Changes what most row-level APIs operate on — the visible rows become tree rows.

inputs.name: enableSubRowSorting
inputs.description: Sorts children within their parent instead of leaving them in source order. Requires {@link localSorting}; the tree shape is always preserved.

inputs.name: enableVirtualScroll
inputs.description: Controls how large datasets are handled. - `true`: Always use virtual scrolling (recommended for 500+ rows without pagination) - `false`: Never use virtual scrolling, use pagination instead (default) - `"auto"`: Automatically enable if rows > 500 or columns > 20 Note: Virtual scroll and pagination are mutually exclusive. When both are enabled, pagination takes precedence unless enableVirtualScroll is explicitly `true`.

inputs.name: expandedRows
inputs.description: Which detail rows are open, keyed by {@link getRowId}. Two-way.

inputs.name: filterDebounce
inputs.description: Milliseconds to wait after typing before the global filter is applied and {@link filterChange} emitted. 0 (default) applies on every keystroke. Only the toolbar's global filter is debounced — column filters apply immediately.

inputs.name: fullWidthRowComponent
inputs.description: Component for a {@link fullWidthRow}; bound `row` and `index` inputs.

inputs.name: fullWidthRowTemplate
inputs.description: Content for a {@link fullWidthRow}, receiving the row as `$implicit` and its rendered `index`. Takes precedence over {@link fullWidthRowComponent}; with neither, the full-width cell renders empty.

inputs.name: getChildren
inputs.description: Reads a row's children. Defaults to the row's `children` property.
inputs.default: (row: T) => (row as Record<string, unknown>)['children'] as T[] | undefined

inputs.name: getRowId
inputs.description: Stable identity for a row, used as the key of {@link rowSelection}, {@link expandedRows} and {@link subRowExpandedRows}. Defaults to the row's `id` property, falling back to `JSON.stringify(row)` when absent — which means edits change a row's identity and drop its selection. Supply a real key whenever rows are editable.

inputs.name: globalFilter
inputs.description: The toolbar's search text. Two-way, so setting it filters programmatically — but writing it directly bypasses {@link filterDebounce}, the page-index reset and the {@link filterChange} emission that {@link onFilterChange} does.

inputs.name: groupAggregates
inputs.description: When true, group header rows display per-column aggregate values.

inputs.name: groupBy
inputs.description: Group rows by this column accessorKey. Renders collapsible group headers with per-group aggregation. Mutually exclusive with `enableSubRows` and virtual scroll (ignored, with a console warning, when combined). In grouped mode inline cell editing, cell-range selection, keyboard cell-nav, and row drag are disabled.

inputs.name: loaderComponent
inputs.description: Component rendered inside the loading overlay. Used only when {@link loaderTemplate} is unset.

inputs.name: loaderComponentInputs
inputs.description: Inputs bound onto {@link loaderComponent}. The table always adds a `trigger` input carrying the current {@link DataTableLoadingTrigger}, overwriting any `trigger` you pass here.

inputs.name: loaderTemplate
inputs.description: Custom content for the loading overlay. Receives the active {@link DataTableLoadingTrigger} as both `$implicit` and `trigger`. Takes precedence over {@link loaderComponent}; with neither, a default spinner is rendered.

inputs.name: loading
inputs.description: Shows the busy overlay above the (still rendered) table. Which triggers actually surface it is filtered by {@link loadingVisibility}, so setting this alone does not guarantee an overlay. Also blocks row drag.

inputs.name: loadingVisibility
inputs.description: Per-trigger opt-out for the {@link loading} overlay: set a key to `false` to keep the table quiet during e.g. sorting round-trips while still showing the overlay on the initial load. Unset keys default to visible.
inputs.default: {    initial: true,    pagination: true,    sorting: true,    filtering: true,  }

inputs.name: locale
inputs.description: Locale dictionary or registry key. Falls back to `UI_LOCALE_ID` when not set. The DataTableLocale covers data-table chrome (filter placeholder, columns menu, sort/pin actions, pagination labels, etc.). Date filters embedded in the table still read from `CalendarLocale` separately.

inputs.name: localFiltering
inputs.description: Filter the rows in the browser — global filter, per-column filters and the advanced filter tree all become no-ops when false. {@link filterChange} still fires so you can filter server-side.

inputs.name: localPagination
inputs.description: Slice the rows in the browser. Set false for server-side paging: supply only the current page in {@link data}, set {@link total} to the full row count, and re-fetch from {@link pageChange}.

inputs.name: localReorder
inputs.description: Applies a completed drag to {@link data} automatically (the default): the drop runs {@link reorderData} and writes the new array back before {@link rowReorder} is emitted, so a handler reading `data()` already sees the moved row. Set it to `false` for server-side or otherwise custom reordering — the table then only emits the event and leaves `data` alone.

inputs.name: localSorting
inputs.description: Sort the rows in the browser. Set false for server-side sorting: the header still cycles and {@link sortChange} / {@link multiSortChange} still fire, but the row order is left exactly as you supply it in {@link data}.

inputs.name: maxMultiSortColumns
inputs.description: Cap on the multi-sort chain; adding beyond it drops the oldest column. Values below 1 are clamped to 1. Ignored unless {@link enableMultiSort}.

inputs.name: multiSortState
inputs.description: The ordered multi-sort chain, highest priority first. Only consulted while {@link enableMultiSort} is on; capped at {@link maxMultiSortColumns}.

inputs.name: pageSizeOptions
inputs.description: Choices offered in the footer's page-size select.

inputs.name: paginationState
inputs.description: Current page index and size. Two-way: the table resets `pageIndex` to 0 whenever a filter changes, so don't assume it stays where you put it.

inputs.name: rowDetailComponent
inputs.description: Component rendered in the detail row when {@link rowDetailTemplate} is unset.

inputs.name: rowDetailTemplate
inputs.description: Detail-row content, receiving the row as `$implicit`/`row`. Takes precedence over {@link rowDetailComponent}.

inputs.name: rowDragMode
inputs.description: `"flat"` (default) allows only above/below drops, and — in tree mode — blocks drops across differing depths. `"tree"` adds an `"on"` position over the middle of a row, which re-parents the dragged node via {@link setChildren}.

inputs.name: rowSelection
inputs.description: Selection as an id → true map keyed by {@link getRowId}. Two-way: the table writes a *new* object on every change. Ids of rows that are filtered out (or no longer in {@link data}) are kept, so selection survives a filter — read it back against your data rather than treating its size as "visible selected".

inputs.name: setChildren
inputs.description: Returns a *new* row with the given children — the table never mutates a row in place. Used when tree row-drag re-parents nodes; the default spreads the row and replaces `children`.

inputs.name: showColumnBorders
inputs.description: Adds the vertical rule between cells. Purely cosmetic.

inputs.name: showColumnVisibilityToggle
inputs.description: Hides the columns popover in the toolbar; only shown when at least one column is hideable.

inputs.name: showFooter
inputs.description: Footer row visibility. `"auto"` (default) shows it only when some column declares a `footer`, `aggregateFn`, `footerTemplate` or `footerComponent`; `true` forces an (otherwise empty) footer.

inputs.name: showPageSizeSelector
inputs.description: Hides the page-size select while keeping the page buttons.

inputs.name: showPagination
inputs.description: Renders the pagination footer. Also acts as a mode switch: with {@link localPagination} on, `enableVirtualScroll: "auto"` declines to virtualize while pagination is showing.

inputs.name: showRowBorders
inputs.description: Adds the horizontal rule under each row/header cell. Purely cosmetic.

inputs.name: showToolbar
inputs.description: Hides the whole toolbar row (global filter, advanced filter, columns menu) when false.

inputs.name: skeleton
inputs.description: Replaces the entire table — toolbar, grid and footer — with placeholder bars. This is the first-paint state, distinct from {@link loading}, which overlays the real table.

inputs.name: skeletonRows
inputs.description: Number of placeholder row bars drawn while {@link skeleton} is true.

inputs.name: sortState
inputs.description: Current single-column sort. Two-way, so writing it sorts programmatically (locally, when {@link localSorting}) — but unlike {@link onSortChange} it emits no {@link sortChange} and does not touch {@link multiSortState}.

inputs.name: subRowDefaultExpanded
inputs.description: Depth expanded on first render (0 = only roots, 1 = roots plus their children, …). It seeds {@link subRowExpandedRows}; explicit entries there win.

inputs.name: subRowExpandedRows
inputs.description: Which tree nodes are expanded, keyed by {@link getRowId}. Two-way, and separate from {@link expandedRows} (which is master/detail).

inputs.name: subRowFilterMode
inputs.description: What a filter match does to the hierarchy — by default a matching child keeps its ancestors visible so it can still be reached.

inputs.name: subRowIndentSize
inputs.description: Pixels of indent added per tree depth level in the first data column.

inputs.name: subRowSelectionMode
inputs.description: How a checkbox click propagates through the tree: `"self"` (default) touches only the clicked row; the cascading modes also select descendants and derive an indeterminate parent state.

inputs.name: subRowsPaginated
inputs.description: Paginate over *visible* (flattened) tree rows rather than over root rows, so expanding a node can push its siblings onto the next page.

inputs.name: total
inputs.description: Full row count on the server. Required — and only used — when {@link localPagination} is false, where it drives the page count and the "N of M" readouts; ignored otherwise, since the local row count is known.

inputs.name: virtualAutoColumnWidth
inputs.description: Estimated width in pixels for 'auto' columns when using virtual scroll. Virtual scroll requires pixel widths for calculations.

inputs.name: virtualAutoThreshold
inputs.description: The row/column counts above which `enableVirtualScroll: "auto"` switches virtualization on. Ignored when {@link enableVirtualScroll} is an explicit boolean.

inputs.name: virtualColumnBuffer
inputs.description: Extra columns rendered either side of the viewport during horizontal virtualization.

inputs.name: virtualRecycleComponents
inputs.description: Reuses cell component instances from a pool as rows scroll instead of destroying and recreating them. Only safe for cell components with no per-instance state outside their inputs. See {@link recycleStats}.

inputs.name: virtualRowBuffer
inputs.description: Extra rows rendered above and below the viewport to hide scroll tearing.

inputs.name: virtualRowHeight
inputs.description: Row height in pixels assumed by the virtual-scroll maths, and the fallback for unmeasured rows under {@link virtualVariableRowHeight}. If your CSS row height differs, the scrollbar and the rows drift apart.

inputs.name: virtualVariableRowHeight
inputs.description: Measures each rendered row and uses prefix sums instead of a fixed row height — needed for wrapping content, at the cost of a `ResizeObserver` per row and re-measurement as rows scroll in.

outputs.name: advancedFilter
outputs.description: Advanced AND/OR filter tree (A5). Applied in addition to global/column filters.

outputs.name: aiFillComplete
outputs.description: Emitted after an AI column-fill completes.

outputs.name: cellEdit
outputs.description: A committed inline cell edit: row, column key, and old/new value. The table has already written the value through the column's `valueSetter` into a new {@link data} array by the time this fires — persist it, and revert `data` yourself if the server rejects it.

outputs.name: cellsPaste
outputs.description: Emitted after a clipboard grid is pasted into cells.

outputs.name: collapsedGroups
outputs.description: Per-group collapsed state, keyed by the stringified group value.

outputs.name: columnFilters
outputs.description: Per-column filter values keyed by accessor key. A value is applied only if the column declares `enableFiltering`; it then runs the column's `filterFn`, or a case-insensitive substring match on the cell's string value. Empty values (null/''/[]) are skipped, so clearing a filter means writing one of those, not deleting the key.

outputs.name: columnOrder
outputs.description: Accessor keys in display order. Keys absent from this array keep their declaration order after the listed ones, so a partial order is legal. Pinned/sticky columns are still grouped to their side.

outputs.name: columnResize
outputs.description: A finished column resize: the column key and its new pixel width. The width is already in {@link columnWidths}, so handle this only to persist it.

outputs.name: columnVisibility
outputs.description: Column visibility keyed by accessor key. Only `false` hides — a missing key counts as visible, so hiding requires writing `false`, not deleting.

outputs.name: columnWidths
outputs.description: Runtime column widths (CSS length strings) keyed by accessor key, overriding each column's declared `width`. Written by {@link enableColumnResize}; a good thing to persist and restore — see {@link getColumnState} / {@link applyColumnState}.

outputs.name: data
outputs.description: The row array. A `model`, and the table *does* write back to it: inline edits committed through a column `valueSetter`, fill-handle, paste and undo/redo all emit a new array here, as does a row drag while {@link localReorder} is on. Filtering, sorting and pagination never mutate it — they derive views.

outputs.name: editError
outputs.description: A rejected inline edit (a column `validate` returned an error). The value is *not* written and the editor stays open with the message shown inline.

outputs.name: editRedo
outputs.description: Fired after a redo has been applied. See {@link editUndo}.

outputs.name: editUndo
outputs.description: Fired after an undo has been applied (the inverse values are already written to {@link data} and re-emitted as {@link cellEdit}). Requires {@link enableEditHistory}.

outputs.name: expandedRows
outputs.description: Which detail rows are open, keyed by {@link getRowId}. Two-way.

outputs.name: fillSeries
outputs.description: Emitted after a fill-handle drag applies values to new rows.

outputs.name: filterChange
outputs.description: The raw global-filter text, after {@link filterDebounce}. Fires even when {@link localFiltering} is false, which is how you drive a server-side search.

outputs.name: globalFilter
outputs.description: The toolbar's search text. Two-way, so setting it filters programmatically — but writing it directly bypasses {@link filterDebounce}, the page-index reset and the {@link filterChange} emission that {@link onFilterChange} does.

outputs.name: multiSortChange
outputs.description: The whole ordered sort chain, highest priority first, after a multi-sort change. Only meaningful with {@link enableMultiSort}.

outputs.name: multiSortState
outputs.description: The ordered multi-sort chain, highest priority first. Only consulted while {@link enableMultiSort} is on; capped at {@link maxMultiSortColumns}.

outputs.name: nlFilter
outputs.description: Emitted after a natural-language query is compiled into a filter.

outputs.name: pageChange
outputs.description: The requested page index/size. Fires for both local and server paging; with {@link localPagination} false this is your cue to fetch the page.

outputs.name: paginationState
outputs.description: Current page index and size. Two-way: the table resets `pageIndex` to 0 whenever a filter changes, so don't assume it stays where you put it.

outputs.name: rangeChartOpen
outputs.description: Emitted when the user opens the range chart; carries the chart payload.

outputs.name: rowReorder
outputs.description: A completed row drag: the moved row plus its source and target indices, in the *rendered* (filtered/sorted/paged) order — map back to your source collection before persisting.

outputs.name: rowSelection
outputs.description: Selection as an id → true map keyed by {@link getRowId}. Two-way: the table writes a *new* object on every change. Ids of rows that are filtered out (or no longer in {@link data}) are kept, so selection survives a filter — read it back against your data rather than treating its size as "visible selected".

outputs.name: sortChange
outputs.description: The new single-sort state after a header activation (direction `null` means the sort was cleared). Fires regardless of {@link localSorting} — handle it to sort server-side.

outputs.name: sortState
outputs.description: Current single-column sort. Two-way, so writing it sorts programmatically (locally, when {@link localSorting}) — but unlike {@link onSortChange} it emits no {@link sortChange} and does not touch {@link multiSortState}.

outputs.name: subRowExpandedRows
outputs.description: Which tree nodes are expanded, keyed by {@link getRowId}. Two-way, and separate from {@link expandedRows} (which is master/detail).

inputs.name: class
inputs.description: Extra classes merged onto the flex container (not onto the button).

inputs.name: column
inputs.description: The column key this header sorts. Purely informational for consumers that host the header themselves — the component never resolves it against data and emits only a direction; the parent table maps it back to a column.

inputs.name: direction
inputs.description: Current sort direction, rendered as the arrow icon. This is a *controlled* input: {@link toggleSort} does not change it, it only emits the next direction, so the parent must feed the new value back in.

inputs.name: enableSorting
inputs.description: When false the header renders plain text instead of a button — no sort affordance, no keyboard target, and {@link sort} never fires.

inputs.name: sortIndex
inputs.description: Zero-based position of this column in a multi-sort chain; rendered as a 1-based badge next to the arrow. `null` (the default) hides the badge — pass it only while the table is in multi-sort mode.

inputs.name: title
inputs.description: Header text rendered in the button, and the prefix of {@link sortAriaLabel}.

outputs.name: sort
outputs.description: The next direction in the asc → desc → null cycle. Emitted on every activation; carries no modifier information — use {@link sortMeta} when you need to distinguish a shift-click multi-sort.

outputs.name: sortMeta
outputs.description: Same direction as {@link sort}, plus `multi: true` when the activating event carried the shift key (a request to *add* to the sort chain rather than replace it). Both outputs fire on every activation, in this order.

inputs.name: class
inputs.description: Extra classes merged onto the panel wrapper (the calendar keeps its own).

inputs.name: locale
inputs.description: Locale dictionary or registry key (BCP-47). Falls back to `UI_LOCALE_ID` when not set — so an embedded date filter inside `<ui-data-table locale="he">` is automatically Hebrew without per-column wiring.

inputs.name: selected
inputs.description: The externally-held selected date. An effect mirrors it into the internal signal the calendar reads, so pushing a new value (or `null`) resets the panel — but the component also updates that signal itself on interaction, so it works uncontrolled if you never write back.

inputs.name: title
inputs.description: Optional heading above the Today/Clear row; omitted entirely when unset.

outputs.name: filterChange
outputs.description: The newly picked date, or `null` when cleared. The component filters nothing itself — pair it with {@link dateFilterFn} as the column's filter function and feed this value in as the column filter value.

inputs.name: class
inputs.description: Extra classes merged onto the panel wrapper (the calendar keeps its own).

inputs.name: locale
inputs.description: Locale dictionary or registry key (BCP-47). Falls back to `UI_LOCALE_ID` when not set — so an embedded date-range filter inside `<ui-data-table locale="he">` is automatically Hebrew.

inputs.name: presets
inputs.description: Replaces the built-in quick ranges (Today / Last 7 days / Last 30 days / This month). An empty array — the default — keeps the built-ins, which are localized from the active {@link locale}; there is no way to render *no* presets.

inputs.name: selected
inputs.description: The externally-held range. An effect mirrors it into the internal signal the calendar reads (`null` becomes an empty `{ start: null, end: null }`), so pushing a new value resets the panel; the component also maintains that signal itself, so it works uncontrolled if you never write back.

inputs.name: title
inputs.description: Optional heading above the preset row; omitted entirely when unset.

outputs.name: filterChange
outputs.description: The completed range, or `null` when cleared. Only emitted once *both* endpoints exist — picking the first endpoint updates the calendar but stays silent — so a consumer never sees a half-open range from calendar clicks. Presets emit immediately. Pair with {@link dateRangeFilterFn}.

classes.name: DataTableFilterBuilderComponent
classes.description: Recursive AND/OR filter-tree editor (A5). Standalone — it lists itself in `imports` so nested groups render the same component.

inputs.name: columns
inputs.description: The columns offered in each condition's first dropdown. A condition whose `column` is not in this list renders with no option selected — the tree is never rewritten to match. {@link addCondition} seeds new conditions with the first entry, so an empty array produces conditions with an empty key.

inputs.name: group
inputs.description: The filter tree to render. Fully controlled: every edit emits a brand-new tree on {@link groupChange} and mutates nothing here, so the builder shows no change until you feed the emitted value back in.

inputs.name: labels
inputs.description: Localized strings; defaults to the English {@link DEFAULT_FILTER_BUILDER_LABELS}.

outputs.name: groupChange
outputs.description: A complete replacement tree emitted on every edit (combinator toggle, add/remove, or any field change), including edits bubbled up from nested groups. The builder evaluates nothing — pass the tree to the data-table's advanced filter to actually filter rows.

inputs.name: class
inputs.description: Extra classes merged onto the panel wrapper (the command palette keeps its own).

inputs.name: displayWith
inputs.description: Maps an option to its visible label, also used as the command item's search text.

inputs.name: locale
inputs.description: Locale dictionary or registry key. Falls back to `UI_LOCALE_ID` when not set.

inputs.name: options
inputs.description: The full option list. Every option is rendered — the search box filters the DOM via `ui-command`, it does not narrow this array, so {@link selectAll} still selects everything regardless of the current search text.

inputs.name: placeholder
inputs.description: Override for the command-input placeholder. Falls back to the locale's `searchPlaceholder`.

inputs.name: selected
inputs.description: Externally-held selection, expressed as {@link valueWith} values (not options). Values are kept as given — one with no matching option yet (or ever) stays selected and is re-emitted with the rest, so `selected` may be set before {@link options} arrives.

inputs.name: title
inputs.description: Optional heading above the palette; when set, a badge shows the selected count.

inputs.name: valueWith
inputs.description: Maps an option to the value emitted on {@link filterChange} and compared against the cell value by {@link multiselectFilterFn}. Comparison is by `Set`/`includes` identity, so object values must be referentially stable — project to a primitive key here for object options.

outputs.name: filterChange
outputs.description: The selected {@link valueWith} values after each toggle, or `null` when the selection becomes empty — `null` means "no filter" to {@link multiselectFilterFn}, so an empty array is never emitted.

inputs.name: ofLabel
inputs.description: The word between current page and total pages in "Page X of Y".

inputs.name: pageLabel
inputs.description: Prefix of the "Page X of Y" indicator.

inputs.name: pageSizeOptions
inputs.description: Choices in the page-size select. A size not in this list still displays, as the placeholder.

inputs.name: rowsPerPageLabel
inputs.description: Label beside the page-size select; hidden below the `sm` breakpoint.

inputs.name: showPageSizeSelector
inputs.description: Hides the page-size select when false; the page buttons remain.

inputs.name: state
inputs.description: The controlled page index + size. Nothing is stored locally: the buttons only emit a new state on {@link paginationChange}, so the display does not move until you feed the value back in.

inputs.name: total
inputs.description: Total row count across all pages (not the current page's length). Drives the page count and therefore the next/last disabled state; leave it at 0 and the control collapses to a single page.

outputs.name: paginationChange
outputs.description: The requested next state, already clamped to `[0, totalPages - 1]`. Changing the page size resets `pageIndex` to 0. The component never paginates data itself — slice your rows from this.

classes.name: DatePickerComponent
classes.description: DatePickerComponent - A date selection component combining Popover and Calendar Usage: <ui-date-picker [(date)]="selectedDate" placeholder="Select a date" /> <ui-date-picker [showTime]="true" placeholder="Pick date & time" /> Or with reactive forms: <ui-date-picker formControlName="birthDate" />

inputs.name: class
inputs.description: Merged onto the trigger button, whose default width is `w-full sm:w-[240px]` — use it to widen/narrow the field or restyle the border. The popup is unaffected.

inputs.name: date
inputs.description: Initial/externally-set date, for `[(date)]` two-way binding with {@link dateChange}. Pushing `null` clears the selection back to the {@link placeholder}; only the initial `null` default is ignored, so a date written through a form control is not clobbered on first render.

inputs.name: disabled
inputs.description: Disables the trigger button and makes {@link toggleOpen} a no-op. Driven only by this input — {@link setDisabledState} ignores `control.disable()`.

inputs.name: locale
inputs.description: BCP 47 tag passed to the calendar and to `toLocaleDateString` for the trigger label — it selects month/day names and field order, not a timezone.

inputs.name: placeholder
inputs.description: Muted text shown on the trigger while no date is selected; replaced by {@link formatDate} output once there is one.

inputs.name: showTime
inputs.description: Adds the calendar's time-of-day selector and includes 2-digit hours and minutes in the trigger label. Also changes dismissal: with time on, picking a day keeps the popup open so the time can still be set, instead of closing on selection (see {@link onDateSelect}).

outputs.name: dateChange
outputs.description: Emits on every calendar selection (the `[(date)]` half). Fires alongside the `ControlValueAccessor` change callback, so forms and two-way binding stay in sync.

classes.name: DateRangePickerComponent
classes.description: DateRangePickerComponent - For selecting a date range Usage: <ui-date-range-picker (rangeChange)="onRangeChange($event)" />

inputs.name: class
inputs.description: Merged onto the trigger button, whose default width is `w-full sm:w-[300px]` (wider than the single picker, to fit two formatted dates). The popup is unaffected.

inputs.name: disabled
inputs.description: Disables the trigger and makes {@link toggleOpen} a no-op. Driven only by this input — {@link setDisabledState} ignores `control.disable()`.

inputs.name: locale
inputs.description: BCP 47 tag passed to the calendar and to `toLocaleDateString` for both trigger labels — it selects month/day names and field order, not a timezone.

inputs.name: placeholder
inputs.description: Muted text on the trigger while no start date is chosen. Once only a start exists the label becomes `<start> - ...`; with both it is `<start> - <end>`.

inputs.name: showTime
inputs.description: Adds the calendar's start/end time selectors (reported through {@link timeRangeChange}, kept separate from the dates) and appends 2-digit hours and minutes to both trigger labels. It also suppresses the auto-close once both ends are picked, so the times can still be set.

outputs.name: rangeChange
outputs.description: Emits the range on every calendar click — including the half-finished `{ start, end: null }` state after the first click — so a consumer must check `end` before treating it as a complete range. Fires alongside the `ControlValueAccessor` change callback.

outputs.name: timeRangeChange
outputs.description: Emits the `HH:mm` start/end times when {@link showTime} is on. Times are tracked separately from {@link rangeChange} and are never merged into the `Date` objects.

inputs.name: open
inputs.description: Two-way bound visibility. The projected `ui-dialog-content` only renders its overlay and panel while this is `true`, so nothing inside the dialog exists in the DOM when closed — bind it if you need to open the dialog without a `ui-dialog-trigger`.

outputs.name: open
outputs.description: Two-way bound visibility. The projected `ui-dialog-content` only renders its overlay and panel while this is `true`, so nothing inside the dialog exists in the DOM when closed — bind it if you need to open the dialog without a `ui-dialog-trigger`.

inputs.name: class
inputs.description: Extra classes merged onto the centred panel (not the backdrop). Overrides the default `max-w-[calc(100vw-2rem)] sm:max-w-lg` sizing when you pass a width utility.

inputs.name: description
inputs.description: Simple-mode sub-heading. Only rendered when {@link title} is also set.

inputs.name: locale
inputs.description: Locale dictionary or registry key. Falls back to `UI_LOCALE_ID` when not set.

inputs.name: title
inputs.description: Simple mode: renders a `ui-dialog-header`/`ui-dialog-title` above the projected content. Leave unset and project your own header for full control — {@link description} is only rendered when this is set too.

inputs.name: locale
inputs.description: Locale used for the floating "Copied" confirmation label. Accepts a built-in locale key or a partial override object; falls back to the library default when omitted.

inputs.name: uiCopyTo
inputs.description: Text written to the system clipboard when the host element is clicked. Evaluated at click time, so a signal/binding here can supply a value that changes between clicks.

outputs.name: copied
outputs.description: Emitted after the clipboard write succeeds, just before the confirmation badge appears. Never emits if the write is rejected (e.g. no permission or a non-secure origin).

inputs.name: class
inputs.description: Extra classes merged onto the dock bar, after the position variant. The bar is already `max-w-[calc(100vw-2rem)]` with horizontal scroll, so it survives narrow phones.

inputs.name: distance
inputs.description: How far, in px, the cursor's influence reaches. Width falls off on a cosine curve from {@link magnification} at the centre to the 40px base at this distance — a bigger value lifts more neighbours at once, it does not make them bigger.

inputs.name: items
inputs.description: Simple mode: renders one item per entry. Ignored entirely once any `ui-dock-item` is projected — custom content wins. An entry with an `href` renders a link filling the item, one with only an `onClick` renders a button, and an entry with neither stays decorative. Both are labelled from `label` for screen readers.

inputs.name: magnification
inputs.description: Peak icon width in px directly under the cursor; items rest at 40px. Values below 40 shrink icons on hover instead of growing them.

inputs.name: position
inputs.description: Where the dock is anchored, which sets its axis and alignment (`left`/`right` stack the items in a column). The magnification follows the same axis, so a vertical dock magnifies the item the cursor is beside rather than the whole column.

inputs.name: class
inputs.description: Extra classes merged onto the icon box. It fills the item, so the icon scales with the dock's hover magnification for free — leave the sizing to the parent.

inputs.name: active
inputs.description: Shows the small "running" dot under the icon. Presentational only — it neither highlights the item nor is tracked by the dock.

inputs.name: class
inputs.description: Extra classes merged onto the item host. Avoid `w-*` here — width is owned by the dock's hover magnification and written as an inline style. Add `group` if you project a `ui-dock-label`, which reveals itself on `group-hover`.

inputs.name: class
inputs.description: Extra classes merged onto the tooltip bubble above the icon. It is `hidden` until `group-hover`, and the dock item does **not** carry a `group` class — so the label stays invisible unless you add `group` to the enclosing `ui-dock-item`. Hover-driven either way, so it never appears on touch; put the name in the icon's accessible name too.

inputs.name: direction
inputs.description: Edge the drawer slides in from, read by `ui-drawer-content` (set it here, not on the content). `bottom`/`top` cap at `max-h-[80vh]` and get the drag-handle bar; `left`/`right` are full-height, 75% wide capped at `sm:max-w-sm`, and mirror automatically in RTL.

inputs.name: open
inputs.description: Two-way bound visibility. While `true` the body is scroll-locked (with padding compensating for the hidden scrollbar) and `ui-drawer-content` renders; nothing inside the drawer exists in the DOM when closed.

outputs.name: open
outputs.description: Two-way bound visibility. While `true` the body is scroll-locked (with padding compensating for the hidden scrollbar) and `ui-drawer-content` renders; nothing inside the drawer exists in the DOM when closed.

inputs.name: class
