inputs.description: Extra utilities for the item's row wrapper, merged through `cn()` so they override the built-in `relative flex gap-4 pb-8 last:pb-0` — this is where you change the gap between dot and content, or the spacing to the next item.

inputs.name: description
inputs.description: Simple-mode body text under the {@link title}, rendered as a muted `p`. Omitted entirely when empty, and ignored in custom mode (see {@link title}).

inputs.name: showConnector
inputs.description: Whether the simple-mode vertical line to the next item is drawn (default `true`). Set it to `false` on the last item, since the line is absolutely positioned from the dot to the bottom of this item and does not stop itself. Ignored in custom mode (see {@link title}).

inputs.name: time
inputs.description: Simple-mode timestamp rendered as a plain `time` element below the {@link description}; pass an already-formatted string — no date parsing or `datetime` attribute is applied. Ignored in custom mode (see {@link title}).

inputs.name: title
inputs.description: Simple-mode heading, rendered as an `h4`. Ignored — along with {@link description}, {@link time}, {@link variant} and {@link showConnector} — as soon as a `ui-timeline-header` or `ui-timeline-content` is projected, because {@link hasCustomContent} then swaps the whole default structure for the projected content.

inputs.name: variant
inputs.description: Colour scheme of the simple-mode dot: `'default'` is a hollow bordered circle, `'filled'`/`'outline'` follow the primary colour, and `'success'`/`'error'`/`'warning'` are status colours. Mirrors {@link TimelineDotComponent}'s variant, and is ignored in custom mode (see {@link title}) — project a `ui-timeline-dot` and set its own `variant` instead.

inputs.name: class
inputs.description: Extra utilities for the `time` element, merged through `cn()` so they override its `text-xs text-muted-foreground`. It renders inline with no `datetime` attribute — set one on the host yourself if the timestamp must be machine-readable.

inputs.name: class
inputs.description: Extra utilities for the heading, merged through `cn()` so they override its `text-sm font-semibold leading-none`. The element is always an `h4`; wrap or replace this component if the surrounding document needs a different heading level.

inputs.name: class
inputs.description: Extra utilities for the timeline's own wrapper `div` (the flex container the items lay out in), merged through `cn()` so they win over the built-in `relative` / `flex` defaults.

inputs.name: orientation
inputs.description: Stacking direction of the projected items: `'vertical'` (default) lays the wrapper out as `flex-col`, `'horizontal'` as `flex-row`. Only the container's flex direction changes — nothing is broadcast to the children. {@link TimelineItemComponent} and {@link TimelineConnectorComponent} keep their vertical geometry (the connector stays a `w-0.5` full-height bar), so a horizontal timeline needs per-part `class` overrides on the items and connectors.

inputs.name: horizontal
inputs.description: Horizontal anchor of the stack (default `'end'`). `'start'`/`'end'` are direction-aware and flip under RTL. The stack is capped at `420px` wide and shrinks to the viewport on small screens.

inputs.name: vertical
inputs.description: Vertical anchor of the fixed stack (default `'bottom'`). Toasts are always appended in arrival order, so `'bottom'` grows downward — newest at the bottom — rather than pushing older ones up.

inputs.name: action
inputs.description: Optional action button. `onClick` is invoked as-is and does **not** dismiss the toast — call `ToastService.dismiss(id)` yourself if the action should close it.

inputs.name: countdownSeconds
inputs.description: Seconds left, ticked once per second by `ToastService`; this component only displays the value.

inputs.name: createdAt
inputs.description: Epoch ms when the toast was raised. Supplied by `ToastService` for elapsed-time maths.

inputs.name: description
inputs.description: Secondary line under the title, rendered at 90% opacity. Plain text only — no markup is interpreted.

inputs.name: duration
inputs.description: Total lifetime in ms. Purely presentational here — it is the denominator of the progress bar; the actual dismissal timer lives in `ToastService`.

inputs.name: loading
inputs.description: Renders a spinner ahead of the title. Set by `ToastService.loading()` / `promise()` while work is in flight.

inputs.name: locale
inputs.description: Locale dictionary or registry key. Falls back to `UI_LOCALE_ID` when not set.

inputs.name: showCountdown
inputs.description: Shows the remaining seconds beside the action label and a draining progress bar. Requires {@link duration}.

inputs.name: title
inputs.description: Bold first line. Omit it for a description-only toast — the row is simply not rendered.

inputs.name: variant
inputs.description: Visual style, which also sets the announcement politeness: `destructive` renders `role="alert"` / `aria-live="assertive"`, while `default`, `success`, `info` and `warning` all use `status` / `polite`. `warning` is deliberately polite rather than assertive: it is the "you may want to know" level, and interrupting whatever a screen-reader user is currently reading is reserved for `destructive`. Raise a `destructive` toast (or set `role="alert"` on a standalone `ui-toast`) for a warning that genuinely must interrupt. `info` and `warning` are also the two variants whose palette is tuned for contrast rather than for matching `success`: white on `blue-600` and `amber-950` on `amber-500` both clear WCAG AA for the 14px semibold title, which white on `amber-500` would not.

outputs.name: closed
outputs.description: Emitted when the user clicks the close button or presses `Escape` on the toast. `ui-toaster` responds by calling `ToastService.dismiss` — a standalone `ui-toast` must remove itself, since the component never hides itself.

inputs.name: ariaLabel
inputs.description: Accessible name for the button — required when the item only projects an icon. Applied to the inner button, since the `display: contents` host strips its own `aria-label`.

inputs.name: class
inputs.description: Extra classes merged onto the item's `<button>`, appended after the group-derived variant/size classes so they win.

inputs.name: disabled
inputs.description: Disables this item only. The parent group's `disabled` disables it regardless of this input.

inputs.name: value
inputs.description: Identifier this item contributes to the parent group's selection, and what the pressed state is derived from.

inputs.name: class
inputs.description: Extra classes merged onto the `<fieldset>` that wraps the items.

inputs.name: defaultValue
inputs.description: Initially pressed value(s), read once in `ngOnInit` — a bare string is wrapped into an array. Later changes are ignored.

inputs.name: disabled
inputs.description: Disables every item in the group; an item may also disable itself independently.

inputs.name: items
inputs.description: Data-driven mode: a non-empty array renders one item per entry and makes projected content be ignored.

inputs.name: size
inputs.description: Item height/min-width preset, read by each item through the group and mirrored to `data-size`.

inputs.name: type
inputs.description: `single` keeps at most one item on (and re-pressing it clears the selection); `multiple` accumulates. Also decides whether {@link valueChange} carries a string or a string array.

inputs.name: value
inputs.description: The selection, as a two-way `model()`, in the shape this component has always emitted: the single selected value (`''` when cleared) in `single` mode, the full array in `multiple` mode. Being a `ModelSignal` is what makes this component a valid Signal Forms `FormValueControl`, and it doubles as the `valueChange` output: Angular derives the output from the model, so there is no separate declaration. A write from outside is normalised into {@link selection} and stays silent; only a user toggle emits. It starts `undefined` rather than empty so that "nobody has written this yet" is distinguishable from "written empty" — otherwise the sync effect, which runs after `ngOnInit`, would clobber the {@link defaultValue} seed. Read {@link selection} for the current selection; this member is the published surface.

inputs.name: variant
inputs.description: Item styling, read by each item through the group: `outline` adds borders plus a shared shadow on the group.

outputs.name: value
outputs.description: The selection, as a two-way `model()`, in the shape this component has always emitted: the single selected value (`''` when cleared) in `single` mode, the full array in `multiple` mode. Being a `ModelSignal` is what makes this component a valid Signal Forms `FormValueControl`, and it doubles as the `valueChange` output: Angular derives the output from the model, so there is no separate declaration. A write from outside is normalised into {@link selection} and stays silent; only a user toggle emits. It starts `undefined` rather than empty so that "nobody has written this yet" is distinguishable from "written empty" — otherwise the sync effect, which runs after `ngOnInit`, would clobber the {@link defaultValue} seed. Read {@link selection} for the current selection; this member is the published surface.

inputs.name: class
inputs.description: Extra classes merged onto the button. The pressed look is driven by `data-[state=on]:*` utilities, so restyle it through that selector.

inputs.name: defaultPressed
inputs.description: Initial pressed state, applied once in `ngOnInit`. This is an *uncontrolled* seed — later changes are ignored, and the component owns the state from then on. Use {@link setPressed} to drive it externally.

inputs.name: disabled
inputs.description: Blocks pointer interaction and dims the control. It does not freeze the state: {@link setPressed} still applies while disabled.

inputs.name: size
inputs.description: Size preset. The variant table carries no utilities for it — the actual dimensions come from the component's density CSS, keyed on this value.

inputs.name: variant
inputs.description: `'default'` is a borderless button that only shows a background when pressed or hovered; `'outline'` keeps a visible border at rest.

outputs.name: pressedChange
outputs.description: Emitted with the new state on every user toggle (click or tap). Not emitted when the state is changed programmatically via {@link setPressed}.

inputs.name: class
inputs.description: Extra classes merged onto the bubble, after the placement classes derived from the parent's `side` — pass positioning utilities here only if you mean to override that placement.

inputs.name: tooltipDisabled
inputs.description: Suppresses opening (hover and touch alike) — use it for a conditional hint. Does not close a tooltip that is already open.

inputs.name: tooltipSide
inputs.description: Preferred side. Unlike `ui-tooltip`, this is only a preference: the bubble flips to the opposite side and is then clamped 8px inside the viewport when it would otherwise overflow.

inputs.name: uiTooltip
inputs.description: Plain-text tooltip label, and the directive's own selector. The bubble is created as a detached `div` appended to `document.body`, so it escapes `overflow: hidden` ancestors — text only, no markup. Read once per open, so changing it while the tooltip is showing has no effect until it reopens.

inputs.name: content
inputs.description: Simple mode: the tooltip text. When set, a `ui-tooltip-content` is rendered for you — leave it empty and project your own `ui-tooltip-content` if you need markup inside the bubble.

inputs.name: delayDuration
inputs.description: Hover dwell time in ms before opening. Applies to pointer hover only — keyboard focus and touch taps open immediately.

inputs.name: side
inputs.description: Side of the trigger the bubble is placed on. Read by `ui-tooltip-content`, which positions absolutely inside this host — there is no viewport flipping here, so a tooltip near an edge can clip. Use the `[uiTooltip]` directive instead when you need auto-flip.

inputs.name: active
inputs.description: Two-way activation flag. Setting to `false` cancels the tour without emitting `done`.

inputs.name: class
inputs.description: Extra CSS classes applied to the floating step card.

inputs.name: finishLabel
inputs.description: Override for the forward button label on the final step. Falls back to `t().finish`.

inputs.name: locale
inputs.description: Locale dictionary or registry key. Falls back to `UI_LOCALE_ID` when not set.

inputs.name: nextLabel
inputs.description: Override for the forward button label on non-final steps. Falls back to `t().next`.

inputs.name: prevLabel
inputs.description: Override for the back button label on non-first steps. Falls back to `t().previous`.

inputs.name: showSkip
inputs.description: Whether the Skip button is shown on intermediate steps.

inputs.name: skipLabel
inputs.description: Override for the skip button label. Falls back to `t().skip`.

inputs.name: steps
inputs.description: Steps shown in order. Missing-target steps are skipped with a warning.

inputs.name: storageKey
inputs.description: Persist "this tour is done" under this key so it does not replay on every visit. `null` (the default) keeps the component stateless — flip `active` yourself and persist however you like; the `done` output still fires either way, so an existing consumer's own store keeps working unchanged. When set, the flag is written on **both** endings (`finished` and `skipped`) — a user who dismissed the tour does not want it again either — and a tour whose flag is already set refuses to start: setting `active` to `true` immediately flips it back to `false` without emitting `done`. Storage is best-effort. In private modes or sandboxed frames where `localStorage` throws, reads return `false` and writes are swallowed, so the tour simply behaves as if it had no key. Call {@link resetCompletion} to let it run again, and bump the key (`'onboarding-v2'`) when the tour's content changes.

inputs.name: targetTimeout
inputs.description: Milliseconds to wait for a step's target to appear in the DOM before giving up and skipping the step. `0` (the default) resolves targets once, synchronously. Raise it for steps whose `beforeActivate` navigates or loads data; per-step `targetTimeout` overrides this.

outputs.name: active
outputs.description: Two-way activation flag. Setting to `false` cancels the tour without emitting `done`.

outputs.name: done
outputs.description: Emitted when the tour finishes naturally or is skipped, with the reason. Not emitted when the parent flips `active` off externally.

outputs.name: stepChange
outputs.description: Emitted whenever a step is activated, with its index.

outputs.name: stepSkipped
outputs.description: Emitted for each step the tour passes over instead of showing.

classes.name: TreeContextMenuDirective
classes.description: Attach a context menu to a `<ui-tree>` element. Right-clicking a tree item opens the provided {@link ContextMenuComponent} at the cursor position and emits {@link TreeContextMenuEvent} with the node data extracted from the DOM.

inputs.name: class
inputs.description: Extra classes for the content slot. The host renders as `contents` and projects its content verbatim, so style the element you project instead — this input exists for API symmetry and is not applied to any element.

inputs.name: class
inputs.description: Extra classes for the trigger slot. The host renders as `contents` and projects its content verbatim, so style the element you project instead — this input exists for API symmetry and is not applied to any element.

inputs.name: class
inputs.description: Extra classes merged onto the built-in combobox trigger button (data-driven mode only).

inputs.name: disabled
inputs.description: Disables the built-in trigger. OR-ed with the forms-driven disabled flag from {@link setDisabledState}, so a reactive-forms `disable()` still wins when this is `false` — see {@link isDisabled}.

inputs.name: locale
inputs.description: Locale dictionary or registry key. Falls back to `UI_LOCALE_ID` when not set.

inputs.name: nodes
inputs.description: Tree data for the built-in popover. Passing a non-empty array switches the component into data-driven mode: it renders its own combobox trigger and a single-select `ui-tree` in the popover. Leave it empty to fall back to projected content ({@link TreeSelectTriggerComponent} / {@link TreeSelectContentComponent}), in which case you drive the selection yourself via {@link select}.

inputs.name: placeholder
inputs.description: Override for the placeholder. Falls back to the locale's `selectPlaceholder`.

inputs.name: value
inputs.description: Selected node key for uncontrolled/standalone use. Any value other than `undefined` (including `null`, which clears the selection) is pushed into the internal state whenever it changes. It does not re-assert itself after a user pick, so a static value will not block selection. Prefer `ngModel`/`formControl` over this input — do not use both.

outputs.name: selectionChange
outputs.description: Emits the selected node keys after every pick. Selection is single, so the array holds at most one key and is empty when the selection is cleared — it is an array only to mirror `ui-tree`'s output. Emitted by both {@link onSelectionChange} and {@link select}, each of which also closes the popover. Not emitted for values arriving via {@link value} or {@link writeValue}.

inputs.name: class
inputs.description: Extra classes merged onto the icon wrapper, after the base `me-2 h-4 w-4 shrink-0` sizing. Host is `contents`, so put layout classes here rather than on the element.

inputs.name: class
inputs.description: Extra classes merged onto the item wrapper, after the base `select-none`. Styling the row itself (hover, selected, focused) is driven by the item's `data-expanded` / `data-selected` / `data-focused` attributes.

inputs.name: hasNested
inputs.description: Overrides child detection. Left `undefined` (the default) the item counts its projected `<ui-tree-item>` children, which reports `false` for a collapsed node whose children are not rendered yet — set this to `true` for lazily loaded branches so the expand chevron and `aria-expanded` still appear. Set `false` to force a leaf.

inputs.name: id
inputs.description: DOM id of the `role="treeitem"` element, defaulting to a generated unique id. The tree points `aria-activedescendant` at this id, so override it only with a value unique in the document.

inputs.name: value
inputs.description: The node's key — required, and the identity used for expansion, selection, focus and every emitted key array. Must be unique across the tree; a duplicate makes both items expand and select together.

inputs.name: class
inputs.description: Extra classes merged onto the label, after the base `flex-1 truncate` — override `truncate` here if long labels should wrap instead of clip. Host is `contents`, so put layout classes here rather than on the element.

inputs.name: class
inputs.description: Extra classes merged onto the `role="tree"` root, after the base sizing/focus-ring classes.

inputs.name: data
inputs.description: Data-driven nodes. When non-empty the component renders the whole tree itself and any projected content is ignored; pass `[]` (the default) to hand-author `<ui-tree-item>` children instead. Nodes are matched by `key`, which is what {@link selectionChange} and {@link expandChange} emit.

inputs.name: initialExpandDepth
inputs.description: Levels of {@link data} expanded on load: `0` (default) leaves everything collapsed, `n` expands parents down to depth `n`, `-1` expands every level. Re-applied — and re-emitted through {@link expandChange} — whenever `data` changes, discarding the user's current expansion.

inputs.name: selectable
inputs.description: Selection mode. `'none'` (default) makes {@link toggleSelected} a no-op and omits `aria-selected` from every item; `'single'` clears the previous key before adding the new one; `'multiple'` accumulates keys and sets `aria-multiselectable` on the root.

outputs.name: expandChange
outputs.description: Emits the full set of expanded node keys after every expand/collapse, including the initial expansion driven by {@link initialExpandDepth} and the `*` keyboard shortcut. Expansion state is owned by the component; this output is a notification, not a two-way binding — drive it back only through {@link expandAll} / {@link collapseAll}.

outputs.name: selectionChange
outputs.description: Emits the full set of selected node keys after every selection change — not just the key that changed — so a `'single'` tree emits a 0- or 1-element array. Never emits while {@link selectable} is `'none'`.

inputs.name: cellRadius
inputs.description: Corner rounding of each rectangle, in px (SVG `rx`). Use `0` for square corners.

inputs.name: class
inputs.description: Extra classes merged onto the chart container, which already carries `relative w-full`.

inputs.name: dir
inputs.description: Layout direction. `'auto'` (default) resolves from the host element's inherited DOM direction after view init; `'ltr'`/`'rtl'` force it. RTL mirrors the layout horizontally, so the largest node sits top-right, and anchors the labels to the right edge of their rectangle. See {@link isRtl}.

inputs.name: groupPadding
inputs.description: Inset applied inside every group before laying its children out, in px, so the group border stays visible around them.

inputs.name: height
inputs.description: Height of the SVG in px, applied literally. Unlike the cartesian charts there is no axis gutter — the plot fills the box.

inputs.name: minLabelHeight
inputs.description: Shortest rectangle, in px, that still gets a label. Below this the label is dropped rather than clipped.

inputs.name: minLabelWidth
inputs.description: Narrowest rectangle, in px, that still gets a label. Below this the label is dropped rather than clipped.

inputs.name: nodes
inputs.description: The hierarchy to lay out. A flat `{ label, value }[]` gives proportional rectangles; adding `children` nests them, and a parent's area is then the **sum of its children**, its own `value` ignored. Missing, negative and non-finite values count as 0 — such a node gets a zero-size rectangle rather than distorting its siblings.

inputs.name: showLabels
inputs.description: Draw each node's label when its rectangle is big enough (see {@link minLabelWidth}/{@link minLabelHeight}). Labels never overflow their rectangle.

inputs.name: showTooltip
inputs.description: Show the shared tooltip for the hovered/focused node. Hover still emits {@link nodeHover} when disabled.

inputs.name: title
inputs.description: Human-readable chart name, used only to prefix the container's accessible summary ("<title>. Treemap with N data points.").

inputs.name: unit
inputs.description: Suffix appended to every rendered value — tooltip and aria-labels alike (e.g. `' MB'`, `'%'`). Written verbatim with no separating space.

inputs.name: width
inputs.description: Fallback width of the SVG user-space coordinate system, in px, used until the host has been measured — from then on the `viewBox` tracks the host's real width. The measurement needs a block-level box, which is why the host is `class: 'block'` and the container `w-full`.

outputs.name: nodeClick
outputs.description: Emitted when a node is clicked, or activated with Enter/Space while focused. `point` is the original {@link TreemapNode} — groups included.

outputs.name: nodeHover
outputs.description: Emitted with the node on hover/focus and with `null` on mouse-leave/blur, so consumers can mirror the highlight.

inputs.name: class
inputs.description: Extra classes merged onto the inline wrapper. Because the text length changes constantly, give the surrounding layout a fixed width if you need to avoid reflow.

inputs.name: cursor
inputs.description: Shows the caret after the text. It blinks only while paused between phrases and stays solid while characters are moving.

inputs.name: deleteSpeed
inputs.description: Milliseconds between characters while deleting — usually set lower than {@link typeSpeed}, since erasing reads better fast.

inputs.name: loop
inputs.description: Cycles back to the first phrase forever. When `false`, the run stops with the last phrase left on screen and {@link complete} is emitted.

inputs.name: pauseDuration
inputs.description: Milliseconds a finished phrase stays on screen before it starts deleting. A further fixed 300ms gap follows deletion, before the next phrase begins.

inputs.name: strings
inputs.description: Phrases typed one after another, each deleted before the next. Read fresh on every tick, so the list may change mid-run. All of them are also exposed to assistive tech at once via `accessibleText` — the animation itself is `aria-hidden` decoration.

inputs.name: typeSpeed
inputs.description: Milliseconds between characters while typing forwards. Read per character, so it can be changed live.

outputs.name: complete
outputs.description: Emitted once the final phrase has been typed, which only ever happens when {@link loop} is `false`. Never emitted for a looping animation, nor when the user prefers reduced motion (the first phrase is then shown at once, with no run at all).

classes.name: VirtualScrollComponent
classes.description: Runway Virtual Scroll - Variable Height & Anchor Support

inputs.name: buffer
inputs.description: Extra rows rendered beyond each edge of the viewport. Higher values trade memory for fewer blank frames during fast scrolling.

inputs.name: columnCount
inputs.description: Number of columns when {@link orientation} is `'both'`: `items` is then read as a flat row-major grid `rowCount = ceil(items.length / columnCount)`. Ignored on the single-axis orientations. A value `< 1` collapses the grid to a single column, so a forgotten binding degrades to a plain vertical list rather than dividing by zero.

inputs.name: hasMore
inputs.description: Whether more pages exist. Set it to `false` at the end of the data and {@link scrollEnd} stops firing, along with the loading row.

inputs.name: items
inputs.description: The full backing list. Only the visible window is rendered, so the array may be very large; rows are keyed by an `id` property when present, so give items stable ids to avoid re-creating DOM as the window moves.

inputs.name: loading
inputs.description: Shows the loading indicator at the bottom and suppresses further {@link scrollEnd} emissions, so a slow page load cannot trigger a second fetch.

inputs.name: minItemHeight
inputs.description: Assumed height in pixels for rows that have not been measured yet. Rows are measured once rendered and the estimate corrected, so this only needs to be roughly right — but a badly wrong value makes the scrollbar jump as real heights land.

inputs.name: minItemWidth
inputs.description: Assumed **width** in pixels for cells that have not been measured yet — the horizontal counterpart of {@link minItemHeight}, and used only when {@link orientation} is `'horizontal'` or `'both'`.

inputs.name: orientation
inputs.description: Which axis (or axes) to virtualize. Defaults to `'vertical'`, which is exactly the original behaviour. See {@link VirtualScrollOrientation}.

outputs.name: cellWindowChange
outputs.description: Emitted in `'both'` mode whenever the 2D window moves. Never fires on the single-axis orientations.

outputs.name: scrollEnd
outputs.description: Infinite-scroll trigger: emitted when the viewport reaches within two rows of the end, and only while {@link hasMore} is true and {@link loading} is false. Set `loading` synchronously in the handler, or it will fire again on the next scroll frame.

outputs.name: scrollState
outputs.description: Richer counterpart to {@link windowChange}: the same window plus its size, the total item count and scroll progress from 0 to 1 — enough to drive a custom scrollbar or position readout.

outputs.name: windowChange
outputs.description: Emitted whenever the rendered index window moves. The range includes the {@link buffer} rows, so it is wider than what is actually on screen.

inputs.name: barRadius
inputs.description: Corner rounding of each bar rect, in px (SVG `rx`). Kept small by default so thin single-unit deltas stay legible; use `0` for square corners.

inputs.name: class
inputs.description: Extra classes merged onto the chart container, which already carries `relative w-full`.

inputs.name: data
inputs.description: The bridge, in left-to-right order — order is the story here, since each bar is stacked on the running total left by the one before it. A bar with `type` omitted or `'relative'` is a delta: it spans from the running total to `running + value`, so a negative `value` draws downward. A bar with `type: 'total'` is a checkpoint: it is drawn from the zero baseline up to `value` and *resets* the running total to that value, so its `value` must be the subtotal you want (it is not computed for you — an inconsistent number silently breaks the bridge). `name` labels the category axis and is the band key, so names must be unique; the optional `color` overrides {@link positiveColor} / {@link negativeColor} / {@link totalColor} for that bar alone.

inputs.name: dir
inputs.description: Layout direction. `'auto'` (default) resolves once from the host element's inherited DOM direction after view init; `'ltr'`/`'rtl'` force it. RTL reverses the band range so the first bar sits at the right edge — the value axis, its tick labels and the connectors are unaffected. See {@link isRtl}.

inputs.name: height
inputs.description: Rendered height in px — unlike {@link width} this is set on the SVG directly and never measured, so the chart gets shorter only if you change it. 12px is reserved at the top and 28px at the bottom for the category labels, leaving the rest for the value scale.

inputs.name: negativeColor
inputs.description: Fill for `'relative'` bars with a negative `value`. Any CSS colour; a bar's own `color` wins.

inputs.name: positiveColor
inputs.description: Fill for `'relative'` bars with a `value` of zero or more. Any CSS colour; a bar's own `color` wins.

inputs.name: showConnectors
inputs.description: Draw the dashed step lines linking each bar's closing level to the next bar's start, which is what reads as a "bridge".

inputs.name: showTooltip
inputs.description: Render the hover tooltip showing the bar's change and its cumulative total. Pointer tracking still runs when off, so {@link hovered} keeps driving the dimming of the other bars.

inputs.name: showValues
inputs.description: Print each bar's raw `value` above the bar. Off by default because the same number (plus the running total) is in the tooltip — see {@link showTooltip}.

inputs.name: title
inputs.description: Human-readable chart name, used only to prefix the accessible summary on the container.

inputs.name: totalColor
inputs.description: Fill for `type: 'total'` bars, deliberately distinct from {@link positiveColor}/{@link negativeColor} so checkpoints read as a different kind of bar.

inputs.name: width
inputs.description: Design width of the SVG user-space coordinate system, in px, and the fallback until the host has been measured. The SVG renders at `width="100%"` and the viewBox follows the measured width, so bands re-flow rather than scale. The host must be a block-level box — an inline-block parent collapses a `width:100%` SVG to the 300px default, which is why the container carries `w-full` and the host `class: 'block'`.

outputs.name: barClick
outputs.description: Emitted when a bar is clicked or activated with Enter while focused. The payload's `point` carries the bar's `name` and its own `value` (the delta, not the cumulative level) plus the {@link data} index; no `MouseEvent` is forwarded.

inputs.name: class
inputs.description: Extra classes merged onto the host card — background, padding and shadow are yours to supply; the component only contributes the rounded, clipped, transformed shell.

inputs.name: intensity
inputs.description: Maximum tilt in degrees reached at the card's edges; the angle scales linearly with pointer distance from the centre. Read live, so it can be animated. Set to 0 to freeze the card flat while keeping the handlers.

inputs.name: perspective
inputs.description: CSS `perspective` distance in pixels for the 3D tilt. Smaller values exaggerate the effect, larger values flatten it — the tilt angle itself is controlled by {@link intensity}.

inputs.name: class
inputs.description: Extra classes merged onto the `relative inline-block overflow-hidden` wrapper. The wrapper clips its children, so give it an explicit height (or font sizing) if the rotating words need more room than one line.

inputs.name: duration
inputs.description: Milliseconds each word stays on screen before the next slides up. Read once in `ngOnInit` — changing it later does not restart the timer. The timer is never started at all when the user prefers reduced motion.

inputs.name: words
inputs.description: Words cycled through in order, wrapping back to the first. All of them are rendered stacked and offset vertically; only the active one is visible. With 0 or 1 entries no timer starts and the value stays put.
